            SETS="$SETS --set clusters.hub.managedNodeGroup.capacityType=$(yq '.hub.managedNodeGroup.capacityType // "ON_DEMAND"' {{.CONFIG_FILE}})"
            echo "$SETS"
          fi
    cmds:
      - task: init
      - task: kind:create
      - task: credentials:setup
      - task: crossplane:helm
      - task: crossplane:providers
      - task: crossplane:provider-config
      - kubectl apply -f {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/abstractions/resource-groups/platform-cluster/templates/ 2>/dev/null || true
      - helm template hub-cluster {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/abstractions/resource-groups/platform-cluster
          --set clusters.hub.region={{.AWS_REGION}}
          --set clusters.hub.clusterName={{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}
          --set clusters.hub.kubernetesVersion={{.HUB_K8S_VERSION}}
          --set clusters.hub.vpcCidr={{.HUB_VPC_CIDR}}
          --set clusters.hub.resourcePrefix={{.RESOURCE_PREFIX}}
          {{.MNG_SETS}}
          | kubectl apply -f -
      - kubectl apply -f claims/
      - kubectl -n crossplane-system wait --for=condition=Ready --timeout=1800s platformclusters.platform.gitops.io/{{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}
      - task: destroy-kind

  hub:destroy-addons:
    desc: Remove all addons from the hub cluster (no git changes needed)
    vars:
      ADDONS:
        sh: |
          ENABLED_LABELS=$(for f in {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/overlays/environments/*/enabled-addons.yaml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] && yq -r '.enabledAddons | to_entries[] | select(.value == true) | "enable_" + .key' "$f"
          done | sort -u)
          REGISTRY=$(yq eval-all '. as $item ireduce ({}; . * $item)' \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/core.yaml \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/gitops.yaml \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/security.yaml \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/observability.yaml \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/ml.yaml \
            {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/registry/platform.yaml)
          echo "$REGISTRY" | yq -r 'to_entries[] | .key + " " + .value.selector.matchExpressions[0].key + " " + (.value.annotationsAppSet."argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave" // "0")' | while read addon selector wave; do
            if echo "$ENABLED_LABELS" | grep -qx "$selector"; then
              echo "$wave $addon"
            fi
          done | sort -rn | awk '{print $2}'
    cmds:
      - task: hub:kubeconfig
      - printf '{{.C_ERR}}▸ Stopping all regeneration...{{.C_RESET}}\n'
      # 1. Delete bootstrap ApplicationSet (preserveResources) to stop recreating bootstrap App
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset bootstrap -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":true}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - sleep 3
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset bootstrap -n argocd --timeout=30s 2>/dev/null || true
      # 2. Delete bootstrap Application (no cascade) to stop syncing bootstrap/ directory
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch application bootstrap -n argocd --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete application bootstrap -n argocd --wait=false 2>/dev/null || true
      # 3. Delete cluster-addons ApplicationSet (preserveResources) to stop generating addon ApplicationSets
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset cluster-addons -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":true}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - sleep 3
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset cluster-addons -n argocd --timeout=30s 2>/dev/null || true
      # 4. Delete cluster-addons Application (no cascade)
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch application cluster-addons -n argocd --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete application cluster-addons -n argocd --wait=false 2>/dev/null || true
      # 5. Delete non-Crossplane addon ApplicationSets in reverse sync-wave order
      - cmd: |
          if [ "{{.ITEM}}" = "argocd" ] || [ "{{.ITEM}}" = "crossplane" ] || [ "{{.ITEM}}" = "crossplane-base" ] || [ "{{.ITEM}}" = "crossplane-aws" ]; then
            echo "Skipping {{.ITEM}} (Crossplane stack — deleted after clusters)"
          elif KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl get applicationset {{.ITEM}} -n argocd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "Deleting {{.ITEM}}..."
            KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset {{.ITEM}} -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":false}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 3
            KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset {{.ITEM}} -n argocd --timeout=180s 2>/dev/null || true
            KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl wait --for=delete applications -n argocd -l addonName={{.ITEM}} --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
          else
            echo "Skipping {{.ITEM}} (not found)"
          fi
        ignore_error: true
        for:
          var: ADDONS
      # 6. Delete clusters (spoke + hub claims cleaned up before Crossplane providers are removed)
      - printf '{{.C_ERR}}▸ Deleting clusters...{{.C_RESET}}\n'
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset clusters -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":false}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - sleep 3
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset clusters -n argocd --timeout=60s 2>/dev/null || true
      - cmd: |
          KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl wait --for=delete applications -n argocd -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=clusters --timeout=600s 2>/dev/null || \
          (KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch application clusters -n argocd --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' 2>/dev/null && \
           KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete application clusters -n argocd --wait=false 2>/dev/null) || true
      # 7. Delete Crossplane stack in reverse wave order (providers still alive for cluster cleanup)
      - cmd: |
          for ADDON in crossplane-aws crossplane-base crossplane; do
            if KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl get applicationset $ADDON -n argocd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Deleting $ADDON..."
              KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset $ADDON -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":false}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
              sleep 3
              KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset $ADDON -n argocd --timeout=180s 2>/dev/null || true
              KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl wait --for=delete applications -n argocd -l addonName=$ADDON --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          done
        ignore_error: true
      # 8. Delete fleet-secrets
      - printf '{{.C_ERR}}▸ Deleting fleet-secrets...{{.C_RESET}}\n'
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch applicationset fleet-secrets -n argocd --type merge -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"preserveResourcesOnDeletion":false}}}' 2>/dev/null || true
      - sleep 3
      - KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete applicationset fleet-secrets -n argocd --timeout=180s 2>/dev/null || true
      # 9. Cleanup remaining applications
      - cmd: |
          for app in $(KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl get applications -n argocd -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' 2>/dev/null); do
            echo "Deleting leftover app $app..."
            KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete application $app -n argocd --timeout=300s 2>/dev/null || \
            (echo "Force-deleting stuck app $app (stripping finalizers)..." && \
             KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl patch application $app -n argocd --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":[]}}' 2>/dev/null && \
             KUBECONFIG={{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig kubectl delete application $app -n argocd --wait=false 2>/dev/null) || true
          done
        ignore_error: true
      - printf '{{.C_ERR}}▸ Cleaning up AWS resources...{{.C_RESET}}\n'
      - aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/config --force-delete-without-recovery --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
      - aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/keycloak --force-delete-without-recovery --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
      - aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/keycloak-clients --force-delete-without-recovery --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
      - rm -f {{.ROOT_DIR}}/private/hub-kubeconfig
      - printf '{{.C_OK}}✓ Hub addons destroyed.{{.C_RESET}}\n'

content.data:
Found the root cause. The error is:

**`VpcLimitExceeded: The maximum number of VPCs has been reached.`**

Your AWS account in `us-west-2` has hit the VPC limit (default is 5 per region). The Crossplane composition can't create the VPC for the hub cluster, so all downstream resources (subnets, NAT gateway, IGW, EKS cluster) are stuck.

**Fix options:**

1. **Delete unused VPCs** in us-west-2:
   ```bash
   aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region us-west-2 --query 'Vpcs[*].[VpcId,Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0],CidrBlock]' --output table
   ```
   Then delete any VPCs you no longer need.

2. **Request a VPC limit increase** via Service Quotas:
   ```bash
   aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase \
     --service-code vpc \
     --quota-code L-F678F1CE \
     --desired-value 10 \
     --region us-west-2
   ```

Once you free up or increase the VPC quota, the Crossplane reconciler will automatically retry and create the VPC, which will unblock the entire chain (subnets → NAT → EKS cluster → PlatformCluster Ready).

So there are 5 VPCs (the limit):

| VPC | CIDR | Identity | Source |
|-----|------|----------|--------|
| `vpc-efa90697` | 172.31.0.0/16 | default | AWS default VPC |
| `vpc-0d0b746cf4acf54ca` | 10.2.0.0/16 | `spoke-prod` | **This platform** (Crossplane tag) |
| `vpc-02eb215a5a5c2b1c3` | 10.2.0.0/16 | `blueprint-construct-dev` | **Leftover** from a previous install |
| `vpc-05f6731b44a82bf10` | 10.0.0.0/16 | `peeks-hub` | **This platform** (Crossplane tag) |
| `vpc-03f6f9615f20101a2` | 10.1.0.0/16 | `spoke-dev` | **This platform** (Crossplane tag) |

The Crossplane composition is trying to create a VPC with CIDR `10.0.0.0/16` for `peeks-hub` — but **it already exists** (`vpc-05f6731b44a82bf10`). The issue is that Crossplane doesn't recognize the existing VPC as its own (the managed resource has no `external-name` annotation linking it).

Wait — looking more carefully, the VPC `vpc-05f6731b44a82bf10` is already tagged `peeks-hub`. So either:
1. It was created by a **previous run** of this same install that got interrupted, and the current Crossplane VPC resource lost its reference to it.
2. Crossplane is trying to create a **second** VPC instead of adopting the existing one.

The **leftover** that's safe to delete is `vpc-02eb215a5a5c2b1c3` (`blueprint-construct-dev`). That's from a different project entirely.

**Recommended fix**: Delete the leftover VPC to free up quota:

```bash
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-02eb215a5a5c2b1c3" --region us-west-2 --query 'VpcEndpoints[].VpcEndpointId' --output text
# Delete any endpoints, subnets, IGWs, etc. first, then:
aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id vpc-02eb215a5a5c2b1c3 --region us-west-2
```

Or if that VPC has dependencies, I can check what's attached to it. Want me to investigate `vpc-02eb215a5a5c2b1c3` dependencies so we can clean it up?

content.data:
Here's the full picture. The 3 VPCs are from a previous run and the EKS clusters are gone, but **AMP (Amazon Managed Prometheus) scrapers** are still active and holding ENIs in those VPCs. You need to delete the scrapers first, then the VPCs can be cleaned up.

**Cleanup order:**

1. Delete the 3 AMP scrapers
2. Wait for ENIs to be released
3. Delete subnets, security groups, then VPCs

Want me to run this cleanup? Here's what it would do:

```bash
# Delete scrapers
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-3b48ecb3-2a8b-41d8-9c99-cd62f1ec58be --region us-west-2
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-4a8c7210-58fa-46c7-9bf9-49c7e70802cc --region us-west-2
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-7add7265-2c4c-4f89-8e9f-d2d7c03b44b1 --region us-west-2
# Then wait ~2-3 min for ENIs to release, then delete subnets + VPCs
```
you do that, and wait in the script to allow for the time to clean up all resources

input.__tool_use_purpose: Delete AMP scrapers, wait for ENIs to release, then clean up subnets/SGs/VPCs
input.command:
set -e

echo "=== Deleting AMP scrapers ==="
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-3b48ecb3-2a8b-41d8-9c99-cd62f1ec58be --region us-west-2 --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "scraper s-3b48ecb3 already deleted"
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-4a8c7210-58fa-46c7-9bf9-49c7e70802cc --region us-west-2 --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "scraper s-4a8c7210 already deleted"
aws amp delete-scraper --scraper-id s-7add7265-2c4c-4f89-8e9f-d2d7c03b44b1 --region us-west-2 --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "scraper s-7add7265 already deleted"

echo ""
echo "=== Waiting for scrapers to delete (checking every 15s, up to 5 min) ==="
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  REMAINING=$(aws amp list-scrapers --region us-west-2 --query 'scrapers[?status.statusCode!=`DELETION_FAILED`] | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [ "$REMAINING" = "0" ]; then
    echo "All scrapers deleted."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/20] $REMAINING scraper(s) still deleting..."
  sleep 15
done

echo ""
echo "=== Waiting for ENIs to release (up to 3 min) ==="
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  ENI_COUNT=$(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=interface-type,Values=amp_collector" --region us-west-2 --query 'NetworkInterfaces | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [ "$ENI_COUNT" = "0" ]; then
    echo "All AMP ENIs released."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/12] $ENI_COUNT ENI(s) still attached..."
  sleep 15
done

echo ""
echo "=== Cleaning up VPCs ==="
for VPC in vpc-05f6731b44a82bf10 vpc-03f6f9615f20101a2 vpc-0d0b746cf4acf54ca; do
  echo "--- Cleaning $VPC ---"
  
  # Delete NAT gateways
  for NAT in $(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" "Name=state,Values=available,pending" --region us-west-2 --query 'NatGateways[].NatGatewayId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "  Deleting NAT gateway $NAT"
    aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id "$NAT" --region us-west-2 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  done
done

# Wait for NAT gateways to finish deleting
echo "Waiting for NAT gateways to delete..."
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  REMAINING=$(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=state,Values=deleting,pending" --region us-west-2 --query 'NatGateways | length(@)' --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [ "$REMAINING" = "0" ]; then
    echo "All NAT gateways deleted."
    break
  fi
  echo "  [$i/20] $REMAINING NAT gateway(s) still deleting..."
  sleep 15
done

# Release EIPs tagged by platform
for EIP in $(aws ec2 describe-addresses --region us-west-2 --filters "Name=tag:platform.gitops.io/cluster,Values=peeks-hub,spoke-dev,spoke-prod" --query 'Addresses[].AllocationId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
  echo "Releasing EIP $EIP"
  aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id "$EIP" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
done

for VPC in vpc-05f6731b44a82bf10 vpc-03f6f9615f20101a2 vpc-0d0b746cf4acf54ca; do
  echo "--- Deleting resources in $VPC ---"
  
  # Detach and delete IGWs
  for IGW in $(aws ec2 describe-internet-gateways --filters "Name=attachment.vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --region us-west-2 --query 'InternetGateways[].InternetGatewayId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "  Detaching+deleting IGW $IGW"
    aws ec2 detach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id "$IGW" --vpc-id "$VPC" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
    aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id "$IGW" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  
  # Delete subnets
  for SUBNET in $(aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --region us-west-2 --query 'Subnets[].SubnetId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "  Deleting subnet $SUBNET"
    aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id "$SUBNET" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  
  # Delete non-main route tables
  for RT in $(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --region us-west-2 --query 'RouteTables[?!(Associations[?Main==`true`])].RouteTableId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "  Deleting route table $RT"
    aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id "$RT" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  
  # Revoke SG rules then delete SGs
  for SG in $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --region us-west-2 --query 'SecurityGroups[?GroupName!=`default`].GroupId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    ING=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids "$SG" --region us-west-2 --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissions' --output json 2>/dev/null)
    EGR=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids "$SG" --region us-west-2 --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissionsEgress' --output json 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$ING" != "[]" ] && aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id "$SG" --ip-permissions "$ING" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
    [ "$EGR" != "[]" ] && aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id "$SG" --ip-permissions "$EGR" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  for SG in $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --region us-west-2 --query 'SecurityGroups[?GroupName!=`default`].GroupId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "  Deleting security group $SG"
    aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id "$SG" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  
  # Delete VPC
  echo "  Deleting VPC $VPC"
  aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id "$VPC" --region us-west-2 2>/dev/null && echo "  ✓ $VPC deleted" || echo "  ✗ $VPC deletion failed (may have remaining dependencies)"
done

echo ""
echo "=== Final VPC check ==="
aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region us-west-2 --query 'Vpcs[*].[VpcId,CidrBlock,Tags[?Key==`Name`].Value|[0]]' --output table

```yaml
spokes:
```

You're right — `| [0]` is a band-aid. If the leftover is picked, you'd get stale endpoints or misconfigured scrapers.

Better approaches:

**1. Sort by creation date and take the newest** — guarantees you get the one from the current run:

```jmespath
workspaces[?alias=='peeks-observability-amp'] | sort_by(@, &createdAt) | [-1].workspaceId
```

**2. Tag workspaces with the cluster identity** and filter by tag — but AMP `list-workspaces` doesn't support tag filtering in the query, so you'd need a `describe` + tag check loop. More robust but verbose.

**3. Clean up duplicates at the start of the install** — add a pre-flight step that detects and deletes stale workspaces before provisioning new ones. This is the most robust approach since it prevents the problem entirely.

I'd recommend **option 3** — add a cleanup step early in the `install` task that removes orphaned AMP/AMG workspaces if the current install is starting fresh (i.e., the hub cluster didn't exist yet). This matches the pattern you already have for VPC cleanup in the `destroy` task.

Alternatively, combine 1 + 3: use "newest" as the query safety net, but also add cleanup logic so duplicates don't accumulate.

# Poll for AMP workspace (up to 30 min — Crossplane provisioning can take time)
        # Use tag-based lookup (crossplane-name) to avoid ambiguity when duplicate workspaces exist
        AMP_WORKSPACE_ID=""
        printf '{{.C_STEP}}▸ Waiting for AMP workspace...{{.C_RESET}}\n'
        for i in $(seq 1 60); do
          for WS_ID in $(aws amp list-workspaces --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query "workspaces[?alias=='{{.RESOURCE_PREFIX}}-observability-amp'].workspaceId" --output text 2>/dev/null); do
            TAG_VAL=$(aws amp list-tags-for-resource --resource-arn "arn:aws:aps:{{.AWS_REGION}}:{{.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}}:workspace/$WS_ID" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query "tags.\"crossplane-name\"" --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "")
            if [ "$TAG_VAL" = "{{.RESOURCE_PREFIX}}-amp" ]; then
              AMP_WORKSPACE_ID="$WS_ID"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -n "$AMP_WORKSPACE_ID" ]; then
            break
          fi
          printf '  [%d/60] AMP workspace not ready yet...\n' "$i"
          sleep 30
        done

content.data:
- cmd: |
          helm template crossplane-base {{.GITOPS_ROOT}}/addons/charts/crossplane-base \
            --set providerConfig.enabled=false \
            --set aws.region={{.AWS_REGION}} \
            --set aws.clusterName={{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}} \
            --set aws.accountId={{.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}} \
            --set providers.family.version=v2.5.3 \
            --set providers.iam.version=v2.5.3 \
            --set providers.eks.version=v2.5.3 \
            --set providers.ec2.version=v2.5.3 \
            | kubectl delete --ignore-not-found --wait=false -f - 2>/dev/null || true
          kubectl -n crossplane-system wait --for=delete podidentityassociations.eks.aws.upbound.io --all --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
          kubectl -n crossplane-system wait --for=delete roles.iam.aws.upbound.io -l platform.gitops.io/role --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
        ignore_error: true
      # Phase 6: Safety net — clean up any orphaned AWS resources
      - cmd: |
          for ASSOC_ID in $(aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}} --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query 'associations[].associationId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
            echo "Deleting orphaned pod identity association $ASSOC_ID..."
            aws eks delete-pod-identity-association --cluster-name {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}} --association-id $ASSOC_ID --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          for ROLE in {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneIAMProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneEKSProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneEC2ProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ESOPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-LBCPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ExternalDNSPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ArgoCDCapabilityRole; do
            for POLICY_ARN in $(aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name $ROLE --query 'AttachedPolicies[].PolicyArn' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name $ROLE --policy-arn $POLICY_ARN 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            aws iam delete-role --role-name $ROLE 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          for POLICY in {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ESOSecretsManagerPolicy {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-LBCControllerPolicy {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ExternalDNSRoute53Policy; do
            POLICY_ARN=$(aws iam list-policies --query "Policies[?PolicyName==\`$POLICY\`].Arn" --output text 2>/dev/null)
            [ -n "$POLICY_ARN" ] && aws iam delete-policy --policy-arn "$POLICY_ARN" 2>/dev/null || true
          done
        ignore_error: true
      # Phase 7: VPC-level orphan cleanup. The Crossplane VPC delete in Phase 4
      # can stop reconciling once the providers are torn down in Phase 5, leaving
      # AWS-side dependencies (ELBs, NAT gateways, VPC endpoints, EIPs, subnets,
      # IGW, route tables, security groups). Tear them down by Crossplane tag so
      # subsequent VPC deletes succeed.
      - cmd: |
          # Find any VPCs tagged by the Crossplane EC2 provider for our clusters
          VPCS=$(aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
            --filters "Name=tag:platform.gitops.io/cluster,Values={{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}},spoke-dev,spoke-prod" \
            --query 'Vpcs[].VpcId' --output text 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$VPCS" ]; then
            echo "No tagged Crossplane VPCs found — skipping VPC orphan cleanup"
            exit 0
          fi
          for VPC in $VPCS; do
            echo "=== Cleaning up dependencies in $VPC ==="
            # ELBs (created by aws-load-balancer-controller, not directly tagged
            # by us, but pinned to the VPC)
            for LB_ARN in $(aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --query "LoadBalancers[?VpcId=='$VPC'].LoadBalancerArn" --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              echo "Deleting ELB $LB_ARN"
              aws elbv2 delete-load-balancer --load-balancer-arn "$LB_ARN" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            # NAT gateways and their EIPs
            for NAT in $(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" "Name=state,Values=available,pending" \
                --query 'NatGateways[].NatGatewayId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              echo "Deleting NAT gateway $NAT"
              aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id "$NAT" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            # VPC endpoints (interface endpoints leave ENIs behind)
            ENDPOINTS=$(aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
              --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
              --query 'VpcEndpoints[].VpcEndpointId' --output text 2>/dev/null)
            if [ -n "$ENDPOINTS" ]; then
              echo "Deleting VPC endpoints: $ENDPOINTS"
              aws ec2 delete-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $ENDPOINTS --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          done
          # Wait for NAT gateways to fully delete (they hold EIPs and ENIs)
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            REMAINING=$(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
              --filter "Name=state,Values=deleting" \
              --query "NatGateways[?contains('$VPCS', VpcId)] | length(@)" --output text 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
            [ "$REMAINING" = "0" ] && break
            echo "Waiting for $REMAINING NAT gateways to delete... ($i/30)"
            sleep 20
          done
          # Release EIPs tagged by Crossplane for our clusters

            | kubectl delete --ignore-not-found --wait=false -f - 2>/dev/null || true
          kubectl -n crossplane-system wait --for=delete podidentityassociations.eks.aws.upbound.io --all --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
          kubectl -n crossplane-system wait --for=delete roles.iam.aws.upbound.io -l platform.gitops.io/role --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || true
        ignore_error: true
      # Phase 6: Safety net — clean up any orphaned AWS resources
      - cmd: |
          for ASSOC_ID in $(aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}} --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query 'associations[].associationId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
            echo "Deleting orphaned pod identity association $ASSOC_ID..."
            aws eks delete-pod-identity-association --cluster-name {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}} --association-id $ASSOC_ID --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          for ROLE in {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneIAMProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneEKSProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-CrossplaneEC2ProviderRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ESOPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-LBCPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ExternalDNSPodIdentityRole {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ArgoCDCapabilityRole; do
            for POLICY_ARN in $(aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name $ROLE --query 'AttachedPolicies[].PolicyArn' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name $ROLE --policy-arn $POLICY_ARN 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            aws iam delete-role --role-name $ROLE 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          for POLICY in {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ESOSecretsManagerPolicy {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-LBCControllerPolicy {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}-ExternalDNSRoute53Policy; do
            POLICY_ARN=$(aws iam list-policies --query "Policies[?PolicyName==\`$POLICY\`].Arn" --output text 2>/dev/null)
            [ -n "$POLICY_ARN" ] && aws iam delete-policy --policy-arn "$POLICY_ARN" 2>/dev/null || true
          done
        ignore_error: true
      # Phase 7: VPC-level orphan cleanup. The Crossplane VPC delete in Phase 4
      # can stop reconciling once the providers are torn down in Phase 5, leaving
      # AWS-side dependencies (ELBs, NAT gateways, VPC endpoints, EIPs, subnets,
      # IGW, route tables, security groups). Tear them down by Crossplane tag so
      # subsequent VPC deletes succeed.
      - cmd: |
          # Find any VPCs tagged by the Crossplane EC2 provider for our clusters
          VPCS=$(aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
            --filters "Name=tag:platform.gitops.io/cluster,Values={{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}},spoke-dev,spoke-prod" \
            --query 'Vpcs[].VpcId' --output text 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$VPCS" ]; then
            echo "No tagged Crossplane VPCs found — skipping VPC orphan cleanup"
            exit 0
          fi
          for VPC in $VPCS; do
            echo "=== Cleaning up dependencies in $VPC ==="
            # ELBs (created by aws-load-balancer-controller, not directly tagged
            # by us, but pinned to the VPC)
            for LB_ARN in $(aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --query "LoadBalancers[?VpcId=='$VPC'].LoadBalancerArn" --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              echo "Deleting ELB $LB_ARN"
              aws elbv2 delete-load-balancer --load-balancer-arn "$LB_ARN" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            # NAT gateways and their EIPs
            for NAT in $(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" "Name=state,Values=available,pending" \
                --query 'NatGateways[].NatGatewayId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              echo "Deleting NAT gateway $NAT"
              aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id "$NAT" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            # VPC endpoints (interface endpoints leave ENIs behind)
            ENDPOINTS=$(aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
              --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
              --query 'VpcEndpoints[].VpcEndpointId' --output text 2>/dev/null)
            if [ -n "$ENDPOINTS" ]; then
              echo "Deleting VPC endpoints: $ENDPOINTS"
              aws ec2 delete-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids $ENDPOINTS --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          done
          # Wait for NAT gateways to fully delete (they hold EIPs and ENIs)
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            REMAINING=$(aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
              --filter "Name=state,Values=deleting" \
              --query "NatGateways[?contains('$VPCS', VpcId)] | length(@)" --output text 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
            [ "$REMAINING" = "0" ] && break
            echo "Waiting for $REMAINING NAT gateways to delete... ($i/30)"
            sleep 20
          done
          # Release EIPs tagged by Crossplane for our clusters

for EIP in $(aws ec2 describe-addresses --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
              --filters "Name=tag:platform.gitops.io/cluster,Values={{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}},spoke-dev,spoke-prod" \
              --query 'Addresses[].AllocationId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
            echo "Releasing EIP $EIP"
            aws ec2 release-address --allocation-id "$EIP" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          # Now drop subnets, IGW, route tables, security groups, then VPC itself
          for VPC in $VPCS; do
            for IGW in $(aws ec2 describe-internet-gateways --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filters "Name=attachment.vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
                --query 'InternetGateways[].InternetGatewayId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              echo "Detaching+deleting IGW $IGW"
              aws ec2 detach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id "$IGW" --vpc-id "$VPC" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
              aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id "$IGW" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            for SUBNET in $(aws ec2 describe-subnets --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" --query 'Subnets[].SubnetId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id "$SUBNET" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            for RT in $(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
                --query 'RouteTables[?!(Associations[?Main==`true`])].RouteTableId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id "$RT" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            for SG in $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
                --query 'SecurityGroups[?GroupName!=`default`].GroupId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              # Revoke rules first (SGs may reference each other)
              ING=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids "$SG" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissions' --output json 2>/dev/null)
              EGR=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids "$SG" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissionsEgress' --output json 2>/dev/null)
              [ "$ING" != "[]" ] && aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id "$SG" --ip-permissions "$ING" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
              [ "$EGR" != "[]" ] && aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id "$SG" --ip-permissions "$EGR" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            for SG in $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups --region {{.AWS_REGION}} \
                --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC" \
                --query 'SecurityGroups[?GroupName!=`default`].GroupId' --output text 2>/dev/null); do
              aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id "$SG" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
            done
            echo "Deleting VPC $VPC"
            aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id "$VPC" --region {{.AWS_REGION}} 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          # Secrets Manager — Crossplane cluster claims also push hub/spoke config
          # secrets that survive the AWS resource teardown
          for SECRET in {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/config {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/keycloak {{.HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}}/keycloak-clients spoke-dev/config spoke-prod/config; do
            aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id "$SECRET" --force-delete-without-recovery --region {{.AWS_REGION}} --output text 2>/dev/null || true
          done
        ignore_error: true
      # Phase 8: Clean up Kind (pass CLEANUP_KIND=true to remove)
      - cmd: |
          if [ "{{.CLEANUP_KIND}}" = "true" ]; then
            kind delete cluster --name {{.KIND_CLUSTER_NAME}}
          else
            echo "Kind cluster preserved. Run 'task destroy-kind' or re-run with CLEANUP_KIND=true."
          fi

describe how spokes when defined in config.local.yaml are applied? is this carried over to the .platform folder?

No, spokes are **not** carried over to `.platform`. Looking at the Taskfile flow:

**In `open-agentic-platform/Taskfile.yml`:**

```yaml
spokes:install:
  cmds:
    - task: agentic:ensure-kubeconfig   # points kubectl at the hub EKS cluster
    - |
      # Reads spokes from open-agentic-platform/config.local.yaml
      for SPOKE in $(yq -r '.spokes | keys | .[]' config.local.yaml); do
        # Applies PlatformCluster claim directly to the hub cluster
        kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
        apiVersion: platform.gitops.io/v1alpha1
        kind: PlatformCluster
        metadata:
          name: ${SPOKE}
          namespace: crossplane-system
        spec:
          region: ...
          clusterName: ${SPOKE}
          ...
        EOF
      done
```

The flow is:

1. `platform:install` → uses `.platform/` (Kind + Crossplane) to provision the **hub EKS cluster**
2. `spokes:install` → runs **directly against the hub EKS cluster** (via `aws eks update-kubeconfig`), applying `PlatformCluster` claims from `open-agentic-platform/config.local.yaml`
3. The hub's Crossplane (installed by ArgoCD on the hub) reconciles those claims and provisions spoke EKS clusters

So spokes are defined in the outer repo's config and applied as Kubernetes resources to the hub — `.platform` is only responsible for bootstrapping the hub itself.

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: fleet-secrets
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true
  generators:
    - matrix:
        generators:
          - clusters:
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  fleet_member: control-plane
          - git:
              repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
              revision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
              files:
                - path: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}fleet/members/*/values.yaml'
  template:
    metadata:
      name: 'fleet-secret-{{ .clusterName }}'
      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          ref: values
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          path: 'platform-charts/fleet-secret'
          helm:
            releaseName: 'fleet-secret-{{ .clusterName }}'
            ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
            valuesObject:
              # Default region for spokes that don't set their own.
              # Hub's region (from cluster secret annotation) — keeps spokes
              # in the hub's region unless the spoke values file overrides.
              region: '{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_region }}'
              hub:
                clusterName: '{{ .name }}'
                accountId: '{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_account_id }}'
                addonsRepoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoURL }}'
                addonsRepoRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoRevision }}'
                addonsRepoBasepath: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoBasepath }}'
                fleetRepoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
                fleetRepoRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
                fleetRepoBasepath: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}'
                domain: '{{ .metadata.annotations.ingress_domain_name }}'
                resourcePrefix: '{{ .metadata.annotations.resource_prefix }}'
            valueFiles:
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}fleet/members/{{ .clusterName }}/values.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/environments/{{ .labels.environment }}/enabled-addons.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/clusters/{{ .clusterName }}/addon-overrides.yaml'
      destination:
        name: '{{ .name }}'
        namespace: argocd
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
      # The aws_vpc_id annotation on the spoke cluster Secret is owned by the
      # platform-cluster Crossplane Composition (sourced from XR status.vpcId).
      # Ignore drift on that single field so selfHeal does not strip it.
      ignoreDifferences:
        - group: ''
          kind: Secret
          jqPathExpressions:
            - '.metadata.annotations.aws_vpc_id'

content.data:
Now I understand the full picture. Here's how it works:

**Spoke addons are driven by the `fleet-secrets` ApplicationSet**, which:

1. Runs on the hub cluster (selector: `fleet_member: control-plane`)
2. Discovers spoke definitions from `gitops/fleet/members/*/values.yaml` via a **git generator**
3. For each member found, creates a fleet-secret Application that provisions a cluster Secret in ArgoCD

**The problem**: The git generator will always find `spoke-dev` and `spoke-prod` in the repo (they're committed files), regardless of whether those clusters actually exist. This means:

- ArgoCD will create Applications targeting those spoke clusters
- Those Applications will show as **Unknown** sync status (cluster unreachable) since the actual EKS clusters don't exist
- The `hub:wait-for-sync` task already handles this — it skips `Unknown` status apps

So **spoke addons aren't exactly "disabled"** — the ArgoCD Applications get created but sit in `Unknown` state harmlessly until the clusters actually exist. They don't cause errors, just noise.

If you want to truly disable them for a hub-only setup, you'd need to either:
- Remove `gitops/fleet/members/spoke-*` from the repo (or the branch)
- Or add a condition/label filter to the fleet-secrets ApplicationSet

Yes. Here's how it works:

1. **`agentic:label-clusters`** task labels all ArgoCD cluster secrets with `enable_agent_platform=true`
2. **`agent-platform-app.yaml`** uses `globalSelectors: enable_agent_platform: "true"` — this tells the ApplicationSet chart to only generate apps for clusters that have this label
3. The ApplicationSet generator uses a `clusters` generator with a `matchLabels` selector filtering on `enable_agent_platform: "true"`

So the `enable_agent_platform` label controls **which clusters** get the agentic platform addons (kagent, litellm, langfuse, etc.) deployed to them. The `agentic:label-clusters` task applies it to all cluster secrets in ArgoCD, meaning all clusters (hub + any spokes) get the agentic components.
agentic:label-clusters task labels all ArgoCD cluster secrets with enable_agent_platform=true - is not this a flaw that argo then drops the label or annotation on the next reconciliation?

Yes, it depends on how the cluster secrets are managed.

**If the cluster secret is managed by ArgoCD itself** (e.g., created by the `fleet-secrets` ApplicationSet via the fleet-secret Helm chart), then ArgoCD's self-heal will reconcile the secret back to what's in Git — **stripping the label** you just added.

**If the cluster secret is unmanaged** (created manually or by an external process like the `hub:seed-secret` task), ArgoCD won't touch it and the label persists.

There it is. The `spoke-dev` secret **is managed by ArgoCD** (tracked by `fleet-secret-spoke-dev` app). So yes, this is a flaw:

- The `agentic:label-clusters` task adds `enable_agent_platform=true` to the secret

- On the next reconciliation/self-heal, ArgoCD will reset the secret's labels to what's defined in the fleet-secret Helm chart — **dropping `enable_agent_platform`**

It works *temporarily* because ArgoCD uses `ServerSideApply` (from the syncOptions) which does field-level ownership. But if the fleet-secret chart explicitly sets labels, it would overwrite.

**The proper fix**: The `enable_agent_platform` label should be added in the fleet-secret Helm chart's values (via `enabled-addons.yaml` or the fleet member values), not applied imperatively after the fact. That way it's part of the desired state in Git.

content.data:
There it is. The fleet-secret chart sets labels from two sources:
- `.Values.labels` — static labels (environment, tenant)
- `.Values.enabledAddons` — each enabled addon becomes `enable_<addon>: 'true'`

And the fleet-secrets ApplicationSet reads `enabled-addons.yaml`:
```yaml
valueFiles:
  - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/environments/{{ .labels.environment }}/enabled-addons.yaml'
```

**The approach**: The open-agentic-platform needs to inject `agent_platform: true` into the `enabledAddons` map. But since the valueFiles path points to the platform repo, you can't add files there from the agentic repo.

**Proposed solution**: Instead of labeling imperatively, have the `agentic:bootstrap` task apply a small patch to the fleet-secret values. But that's fragile too.

**Cleanest approach**: Change the `agent-platform-app.yaml` to **not rely on the label at all**. Since the agentic platform is bootstrapped as its own standalone Application (not via the fleet-secrets mechanism), it can simply target all clusters — or use a different selector that's already present.

Looking at the current `agent-platform-app.yaml`:
```yaml
globalSelectors:
  enable_agent_platform: "true"
```

**Option 1: Drop the selector entirely** — target all clusters:
```yaml
globalSelectors: {}
```

**Option 2: Use an existing label** like `fleet_member: control-plane` for hub-only, or `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster` for all.

**Option 3: Have the agentic bootstrap create a ConfigMap or label via a pre-sync hook**, but that's over-engineering.

**My recommendation**: **Option 1** — remove the `globalSelectors` filter. The `agentic:label-clusters` task already labels *all* cluster secrets anyway, so the filter adds no value. If you want to selectively target clusters in the future, you can add the label to the fleet-secret chart's `enabled-addons.yaml` in the platform repo at that point.

This eliminates the race condition entirely — no imperative labeling needed, no risk of ArgoCD stripping it.
agentic:label-clusters - how does it label clusters? does not that have the same flaw that whatever it does will be overwritten by argo?

Yes, exactly the same flaw. Here's what it does:

```yaml
agentic:label-clusters:
  cmds:
    - |
      for secret in $(kubectl get secrets -n argocd -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster -o name); do
        kubectl label -n argocd "$secret" enable_agent_platform=true --overwrite
      done
```

It imperatively labels the secrets. Since those secrets are managed by the `fleet-secret-*` ArgoCD apps (with `selfHeal: true`), ArgoCD will eventually reconcile them back to the desired state defined in Git — **stripping the label**.

It "works" today likely because:
1. ArgoCD uses ServerSideApply, and the field manager for the label (`kubectl-label`) differs from ArgoCD's manager — so ArgoCD may not consider it a drift
2. Or the self-heal hasn't triggered yet on that specific field

But it's fragile and not guaranteed to persist.

**The fix is what I suggested**: remove `globalSelectors` from `agent-platform-app.yaml` and delete the `agentic:label-clusters` task entirely. The agentic platform bootstrap is already a standalone Application targeting the hub by `name: ${HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}` in its destination — it doesn't actually need a label-based cluster selector to function.

If you later want per-cluster opt-in, the proper path is adding `agent_platform: true` to the platform repo's `enabled-addons.yaml` for each environment.
what if I want to have a selector of sorts. Let's say in the config.local.yaml I want to say target spokes for example but not hub, how to do that?

The problem is: the label must live on the cluster secret, and the cluster secret is managed by ArgoCD (fleet-secret chart). You can't imperatively label it without ArgoCD potentially reverting it.

**Approach: Inject the label through the fleet-secret chart's values pipeline.**

The fleet-secrets ApplicationSet already reads overlay files per-cluster:
```yaml
valueFiles:
  - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/clusters/{{ .clusterName }}/addon-overrides.yaml'
```

But that path is in the **platform repo**. You need a way to inject values from the **agentic repo**.

**Proposed solution: Use the `agentic:bootstrap` to create an ArgoCD Application that patches the cluster secrets via a Helm chart in the agentic repo.**

Here's a cleaner design:

**1. In `config.local.yaml`:**
```yaml
agenticTargets:
  - spoke-dev
  - spoke-prod
  # omit peeks-hub = hub doesn't get agentic addons
```

**2. The `agentic:bootstrap` task creates a small "labeler" Application** that deploys a Helm chart from the agentic repo. This chart renders cluster secrets (type `Opaque`, same name) with **only** the label — using ServerSideApply, ArgoCD becomes the field manager for that label and won't fight itself:

```yaml
# gitops/addons/charts/agent-platform-targets/templates/labels.yaml
{{- range .Values.targets }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ . }}
  namespace: argocd
  labels:
    enable_agent_platform: "true"
---
{{- end }}
```

With `syncOptions: [ServerSideApply=true]`, ArgoCD will **merge** the label into the existing secret without overwriting other fields. The fleet-secret app manages its own fields, and this app manages `enable_agent_platform`. No conflict.

**3. The `agent-platform-app.yaml` keeps `globalSelectors: enable_agent_platform: "true"`** — it only targets clusters that the labeler app has marked.

**4. `agentic:label-clusters` is replaced** by this declarative approach. The bootstrap task passes the target list from `config.local.yaml` into the labeler chart's values.

This way:
- Labels are managed declaratively by ArgoCD (not imperatively by kubectl)
- Two ArgoCD apps co-own the same Secret via ServerSideApply (each owns different fields)
- Targeting is driven by `config.local.yaml` in the agentic repo

     - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/clusters/{{ .clusterName }}/addon-overrides.yaml'

That's a much better approach — redirect `fleetRepoBasepath` (and `fleetRepoURL`/`fleetRepoRevision`) to point at the open-agentic-platform repo. Then the fleet-secrets ApplicationSet reads overlays (including `enabled-addons.yaml`) from **your** repo, giving you full control over which addons/labels each cluster gets.

But there's a subtlety: the `fleetRepo*` annotations live on the **hub cluster secret**, which is seeded by the `hub:seed-secret` task in the platform's Kind-Crossplane Taskfile. Currently it sets them to the platform repo:

```yaml
fleetRepoURL: "{{.REPO_URL}}"        # appmod-blueprints
fleetRepoRevision: "{{.REPO_REVISION}}"
fleetRepoBasepath: "{{.REPO_BASEPATH}}"  # gitops/
```

You'd need to override these to point to open-agentic-platform. Looking at your `config.local.yaml`, you already have:

```yaml
agenticRepo:
  url: "https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-open-agentic-platform.git"
  revision: "feature/refactor-agent-platform"
  basepath: "gitops/addons/"
```

You could add fleet-specific overrides, or repurpose the fleet annotations on the hub secret to point to the agentic repo. Then you'd provide `overlays/environments/control-plane/enabled-addons.yaml`, `overlays/clusters/spoke-dev/addon-overrides.yaml`, etc. in the open-agentic-platform repo.

**The catch**: the fleet-secrets ApplicationSet also uses `fleetRepoBasepath` for discovering fleet members (`fleet/members/*/values.yaml`). If you redirect it to the agentic repo, you'd need to provide those fleet member definitions there too — which is actually what you want since you're controlling which spokes exist from the agentic repo anyway.

This effectively makes open-agentic-platform the **fleet control plane** and appmod-blueprints just the **cluster provisioner**. Clean separation.
Okay let's do it but validate first that with the fleet management I will also gain ability to add agentic platform to the  environments of choice

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: fleet-secrets
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true
  generators:
    - matrix:
        generators:
          - clusters:
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  fleet_member: control-plane
          - git:
              repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
              revision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
              files:
                - path: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}fleet/members/*/values.yaml'
  template:
    metadata:
      name: 'fleet-secret-{{ .clusterName }}'
      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          ref: values
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          path: 'platform-charts/fleet-secret'
          helm:
            releaseName: 'fleet-secret-{{ .clusterName }}'
            ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
            valuesObject:
              # Default region for spokes that don't set their own.
              # Hub's region (from cluster secret annotation) — keeps spokes
              # in the hub's region unless the spoke values file overrides.
              region: '{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_region }}'
              hub:
                clusterName: '{{ .name }}'
                accountId: '{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_account_id }}'
                addonsRepoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoURL }}'
                addonsRepoRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoRevision }}'
                addonsRepoBasepath: '{{ .metadata.annotations.addonsRepoBasepath }}'
                fleetRepoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
                fleetRepoRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
                fleetRepoBasepath: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}'
                domain: '{{ .metadata.annotations.ingress_domain_name }}'
                resourcePrefix: '{{ .metadata.annotations.resource_prefix }}'
            valueFiles:
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}fleet/members/{{ .clusterName }}/values.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/environments/{{ .labels.environment }}/enabled-addons.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/clusters/{{ .clusterName }}/addon-overrides.yaml'
      destination:
        name: '{{ .name }}'
        namespace: argocd
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
      # The aws_vpc_id annotation on the spoke cluster Secret is owned by the
      # platform-cluster Crossplane Composition (sourced from XR status.vpcId).
      # Ignore drift on that single field so selfHeal does not strip it.
      ignoreDifferences:
        - group: ''
          kind: Secret
          jqPathExpressions:
            - '.metadata.annotations.aws_vpc_id'

content.data:
Now let me check how the fleet-secret chart uses `enabledAddons` to set labels:

Looking back at the `cluster-secret.yaml` template I already read:

```yaml
labels:
  argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster
  {{- range $key, $val := .Values.labels }}
  {{ $key }}: {{ $val | quote }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- range $addon, $enabled := .Values.enabledAddons }}
  {{- if $enabled }}
  enable_{{ $addon }}: 'true'
  {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
```

So `enabledAddons.agent_platform: true` in the `enabled-addons.yaml` would produce the label `enable_agent_platform: 'true'` on the cluster secret.

**Validation complete.** Here's the chain:

1. `fleetRepoURL`/`fleetRepoBasepath` on the hub secret → points to open-agentic-platform repo
2. Fleet-secrets ApplicationSet reads `fleet/members/*/values.yaml` from that repo → discovers spokes
3. For each spoke, reads `overlays/environments/<env>/enabled-addons.yaml` from that repo
4. The fleet-secret chart renders `enabledAddons` as `enable_<addon>: 'true'` labels on the cluster secret
5. The `agent-platform-app.yaml` ApplicationSet uses `globalSelectors: enable_agent_platform: "true"` → only targets clusters with that label

**So yes** — by providing `enabled-addons.yaml` per environment in the open-agentic-platform repo, you control which clusters get `enable_agent_platform: true`. For example:

```yaml
# open-agentic-platform/gitops/overlays/environments/dev/enabled-addons.yaml
enabledAddons:
  agent_platform: true
  # ... other spoke addons
```

```yaml
# open-agentic-platform/gitops/overlays/environments/control-plane/enabled-addons.yaml
enabledAddons:
  agent_platform: false   # hub doesn't get agentic addons
  # ... hub addons
```

This gives you per-environment opt-in/opt-out of the agentic platform, fully declarative, no imperative labeling, no ArgoCD conflicts.

content.data:
Now let me look at how `platform:configure` generates the `.platform/config.local.yaml` — specifically what it sets for `repo`:

Looking at the outer Taskfile (already read), the `platform:configure` task generates:
```yaml
repo:
  url: "{{.PLATFORM_REPO}}"
  revision: "{{.PLATFORM_REF}}"
  basepath: "gitops/"
```

And in the Kind-Crossplane Taskfile, `REPO_URL`, `REPO_REVISION`, `REPO_BASEPATH` are derived from this config and used for both `addonsRepo*` and `fleetRepo*` annotations on the hub secret.

I need to:
1. Add a `fleetRepo` config to the platform's `config.local.yaml` that points to the agentic repo
2. Have the `hub:seed-secret` use separate values for fleet annotations

content.data:
Now for the control-plane (hub) — the hub secret is managed differently (by External Secrets + seed-secret), but the fleet-secrets ApplicationSet also reads this for the hub if it's a fleet member. Let me check if the hub is also a fleet member in this context:

The fleet-secrets ApplicationSet discovers members from `fleet/members/*/values.yaml`. Since we're only putting `spoke-dev` and `spoke-prod` there, the hub won't be affected by these overlays. The hub's labels come from the `hub:seed-secret` task directly.

But we should still create a control-plane overlay for completeness (the hub-fleet-secret ApplicationSet reads it):

content.data:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: hub-fleet-secret
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true
  generators:
    - clusters:
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            fleet_member: control-plane
  template:
    metadata:
      name: 'fleet-secret-{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_cluster_name }}'
      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          ref: values
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoRevision }}'
          path: 'platform-charts/fleet-secret'
          helm:
            releaseName: 'fleet-secret-{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_cluster_name }}'
            ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
            valuesObject:
              mode: externalSecret
              clusterName: '{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_cluster_name }}'
              externalSecret:
                enabled: true
                creationPolicy: Merge
            valueFiles:
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}fleet/hub/values.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/environments/control-plane/enabled-addons.yaml'
              - '$values/{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoBasepath }}overlays/clusters/{{ .metadata.annotations.aws_cluster_name }}/addon-overrides.yaml'
      destination:
        name: '{{ .name }}'
        namespace: argocd
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true

content.data:
Done. Here's a summary of all changes:

**open-agentic-platform (this repo controls fleet targeting):**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `gitops/fleet/hub/values.yaml` | Hub fleet member config (ExternalSecret mode) |
| `gitops/fleet/members/spoke-dev/values.yaml` | Spoke-dev fleet member definition |
| `gitops/fleet/members/spoke-prod/values.yaml` | Spoke-prod fleet member definition |
| `gitops/overlays/environments/control-plane/enabled-addons.yaml` | Hub gets `agent_platform: true` |
| `gitops/overlays/environments/dev/enabled-addons.yaml` | Dev spokes get `agent_platform: true` + base addons |
| `gitops/overlays/environments/prod/enabled-addons.yaml` | Prod spokes get `agent_platform: true` + base addons |
| `Taskfile.yml` | Passes `fleetRepo` config to platform; removed `agentic:label-clusters` |

**appmod-blueprints (platform repo):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cluster-providers/kind-crossplane/Taskfile.yaml` | Added `FLEET_REPO_*` vars (fallback to `repo.*`); updated `hub:seed-secret` and `secrets-manager:seed` to use them |

**How it works now:**
1. `platform:configure` writes `fleetRepo: {url, revision, basepath}` pointing to the agentic repo
2. Platform seeds the hub cluster secret with separate `fleetRepoURL`/`fleetRepoRevision`/`fleetRepoBasepath` annotations
3. The `fleet-secrets` and `hub-fleet-secret` ApplicationSets read fleet members and overlays from the **agentic repo**
4. `enabled-addons.yaml` in the agentic repo sets `agent_platform: true` → fleet-secret chart renders `enable_agent_platform: 'true'` label on cluster secrets
5. `agent-platform-app.yaml` targets clusters with that label — fully declarative, no imperative labeling

**To opt out a cluster**: just set `agent_platform: false` (or remove it) in the corresponding environment's `enabled-addons.yaml`.
explain the change in the appmod-blueprints repo in the taskfile

The change in `appmod-blueprints/cluster-providers/kind-crossplane/Taskfile.yaml` does one thing: **separates fleet repo coordinates from addons repo coordinates**.

**Before:** The Taskfile had 3 vars (`REPO_URL`, `REPO_REVISION`, `REPO_BASEPATH`) derived from `config.local.yaml`'s `repo:` section, and used them for **both** `addonsRepo*` and `fleetRepo*` annotations — meaning addons and fleet management always came from the same repo.

**After:** Added 3 new vars:

```yaml
FLEET_REPO_URL:
  sh: yq '.fleetRepo.url // .repo.url' {{.CONFIG_FILE}}
FLEET_REPO_REVISION:
  sh: yq '.fleetRepo.revision // .repo.revision' {{.CONFIG_FILE}}
FLEET_REPO_BASEPATH:
  sh: yq '.fleetRepo.basepath // .repo.basepath' {{.CONFIG_FILE}}
```

These read from `config.local.yaml`'s `fleetRepo:` section, **falling back to `repo:`** if `fleetRepo` isn't defined. This means:

- **Existing users** (no `fleetRepo` in config) → behavior is unchanged, both point to the same repo
- **open-agentic-platform users** (has `fleetRepo` pointing to the agentic repo) → fleet management (member discovery, enabled-addons overlays, cluster labels) comes from the agentic repo while addons charts still come from appmod-blueprints

The two places these vars are used:

1. **`hub:seed-secret`** — the initial cluster secret applied to the hub via kubectl. Now uses `FLEET_REPO_URL`/etc for the `fleetRepoURL`/`fleetRepoRevision`/`fleetRepoBasepath` annotations.

2. **`secrets-manager:seed`** — the Secrets Manager secret that External Secrets syncs into the hub. Same split in the metadata JSON blob.

That's it. A backward-compatible change that lets an external repo take over fleet management.

Here's the PR description:

---

**Title:** `feat: Decouple fleet repo from addons repo and fix observability cleanup`

**Description:**

## Summary

This PR makes two improvements to the Kind-Crossplane cluster provider:

1. **Separate fleet repo configuration** — allows an external repo (e.g., open-agentic-platform) to manage fleet membership, cluster targeting, and addon enablement overlays independently from the platform addons repo.

2. **Fix observability resource cleanup** — the `destroy` task now properly cleans up AMP/AMG workspaces and scrapers, and the `seed-observability` task correctly identifies workspaces using Crossplane tags instead of name-only queries.

## Changes

### Fleet repo decoupling

- Added `FLEET_REPO_URL`, `FLEET_REPO_REVISION`, `FLEET_REPO_BASEPATH` vars with fallback to `repo.*` (backward compatible — existing users without `fleetRepo` in config are unaffected)
- `hub:seed-secret` now writes separate `fleetRepoURL`/`fleetRepoRevision`/`fleetRepoBasepath` annotations on the hub cluster secret
- `secrets-manager:seed` uses the fleet vars in the Secrets Manager metadata JSON

This enables the pattern where:
- `addonsRepo*` → points to appmod-blueprints (addon charts, bootstrap)
- `fleetRepo*` → points to an external repo that controls fleet members, `enabled-addons.yaml` overlays, and per-cluster addon targeting

### Observability workspace lookup (seed-observability)

- **AMP**: Now uses `crossplane-name` tag (`list-tags-for-resource`) to identify the correct workspace instead of relying on alias alone. Prevents `ValidationException: Invalid workspaceId` when duplicate workspaces exist from previous runs.
- **AMG**: Same tag-based approach using `describe-workspace` to check `workspace.tags.crossplane-name`.

### Destroy task — observability cleanup (new Phase 7)

Previously, `task destroy` did not clean up AMP scrapers, AMP workspaces, or AMG workspaces. This left orphaned resources that:
- Held ENIs in VPCs (blocking VPC deletion)
- Caused duplicate workspace errors on subsequent installs

New Phase 7 (before VPC cleanup):
- Deletes AMP scrapers matching `<resourcePrefix>-*` alias
- Deletes AMP workspace by `crossplane-name` tag
- Deletes AMG workspace by `crossplane-name` tag
- Waits for scrapers to fully delete before proceeding to VPC cleanup

### Secrets Manager cleanup

- Added `<hub>/secrets`, `spoke-dev/secrets`, `spoke-prod/secrets` to the destroy cleanup list (observability credentials were previously orphaned)

## Testing

- Validated end-to-end install with `fleetRepo` pointing to an external repo

metadata:

          - git:

      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'

          ref: values
        - repoURL: '{{ .metadata.annotations.fleetRepoURL }}'

Yes — the bootstrap app is broken right now. It's looking for `gitops/bootstrap` in the agentic repo (which doesn't have it).

You need to:

1. Push the fix to appmod-blueprints
2. Pull into `.platform`
3. **Re-apply the root-appset** to the hub to fix the bootstrap app:

```bash
cd .platform
git pull origin feature/agent-platform-shapirov
KUBECONFIG=private/hub-kubeconfig task kind-crossplane:hub:apply-root-appset
```

Or more directly:

```bash
kubectl apply -f .platform/gitops/bootstrap/root-appset.yaml
```

This will update the bootstrap ApplicationSet to use `addonsRepoURL` for the bootstrap directory, which still points to appmod-blueprints. Once that's applied, the bootstrap app will recover and sync the corrected `fleet-secrets.yaml`, `hub-fleet-secret.yaml`, and `clusters.yaml` from Git.

So yes — push first, then re-apply root-appset. That's the missing step.
so it will fix the issue to the best of your knowledge

Yes. The chain after the fix:

1. `root-appset.yaml` → uses `addonsRepoURL` → finds `gitops/bootstrap/` in appmod-blueprints ✓
2. Bootstrap app syncs the corrected `fleet-secrets.yaml`, `hub-fleet-secret.yaml`, `clusters.yaml`
3. Those ApplicationSets use `addonsRepoURL` for charts, `fleetRepoURL` for fleet data
4. Fleet data (members, overlays, valueFiles) comes from open-agentic-platform ✓
5. Charts (`platform-charts/fleet-secret`, `abstractions/resource-groups/platform-cluster`) come from appmod-blueprints ✓
6. `enabled-addons.yaml` with `agent_platform: true` flows through → label appears on cluster secrets ✓
7. `agent-platform-app.yaml` targets clusters with that label ✓

The only thing I can't fully verify without seeing it run is whether the `$values/` ref resolution works correctly when the `ref: values` source points to a different repo than the chart source. But this is a supported ArgoCD multi-source pattern — the `$values/` prefix resolves against whichever source has `ref: values`, regardless of which source has the chart.

what is this change exactly?

That's the `root-appset.yaml` — the **very first** ApplicationSet applied to the hub. It creates the `bootstrap` Application which syncs the `gitops/bootstrap/` directory (containing `fleet-secrets.yaml`, `hub-fleet-secret.yaml`, `clusters.yaml`, `addons.yaml`, etc.) into ArgoCD.

Those bootstrap files are platform infrastructure — they live in **appmod-blueprints**, not in the fleet/agentic repo. So the source must point to `addonsRepoURL` (appmod-blueprints) rather than `fleetRepoURL` (open-agentic-platform).

Before this change, `addonsRepo` and `fleetRepo` were always the same URL, so it didn't matter which one was used. Now that they're decoupled, it matters.
but addonsRepo - some addons should come from appmod-blueprints, and some from agentic  - is that holding true?

Yes, and they're handled by **two separate Application paths**:

1. **Platform addons** (ArgoCD, Crossplane, Keycloak, ESO, etc.) — managed by the `addons.yaml` bootstrap ApplicationSet, which uses `addonsRepoURL` → appmod-blueprints. These are the base platform.

2. **Agentic addons** (kagent, litellm, langfuse, agent-gateway, etc.) — managed by the `agent-platform-app.yaml` Application, which uses its own `REPO_URL` (the agentic repo) directly. This is a standalone Application you apply via `agentic:bootstrap` — it's **not** discovered through the bootstrap directory.

So the split is:
- `addonsRepoURL` → appmod-blueprints → platform addons + bootstrap infrastructure
- `agenticRepo` (via `agent-platform-app.yaml`) → open-agentic-platform → agentic addons
- `fleetRepoURL` → open-agentic-platform → fleet members, overlays, enabled-addons targeting

The agentic addons don't go through the `addonsRepoURL` path at all — they have their own independent Application with their own repo reference.

# Agent Platform GitOps Deployment Guide

Deploy the AI agent platform on an EKS cluster using the ArgoCD EKS Capability.

## What Gets Deployed

| Wave | Addon | Source | Namespace |
|------|-------|--------|-----------|
| 2 | kagent-crds | OCI: `ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/helm/kagent-crds:0.7.9` | kagent |
| 3 | kagent (operator + UI) | OCI: `ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/helm/kagent:0.7.9` | kagent |

| 3 | litellm (LLM gateway) | Local chart | kagent |
| 4 | crossplane-agentcore | Local chart | crossplane-system |
| 5 | langfuse (LLM tracing + PostgreSQL) | Local chart | langfuse |

| 5 | prometheus-operator-crds | Helm: `prometheus-community/prometheus-operator-crds:28.0.1` | kagent |
| 6 | kagent-monitoring (ServiceMonitor) | Local chart | kagent |
| 7 | gateway-api-crds | Local chart (Job) | agentgateway-system |
| 7 | agentgateway-crds | OCI: `cr.agentgateway.dev/charts/agentgateway-crds:v1.1.0` | agentgateway-system |
| 8 | agentgateway (control plane) | OCI: `cr.agentgateway.dev/charts/agentgateway:v1.1.0` | agentgateway-system |
| 9 | agent-gateway (Gateway + Policies) | Local chart | agent-core-infra |

### AgentCore via Crossplane (wave 4)

The `crossplane-agentcore` chart provisions Bedrock AgentCore resources using Crossplane compositions:

- **Provider**: `provider-aws-bedrockagentcore` (v2.5.3) with its own Pod Identity
- **XRDs**: `AgentCoreMemory`, `AgentCoreBrowser`, `AgentCoreCodeInterpreter`
- **Compositions**: Pipeline mode using `function-patch-and-transform`
- **Claims**: Create Memory, Browser, and Code Interpreter with cluster-unique names (`{clusterName}_{projectName}_{type}`)

Prerequisites: Crossplane must be installed with `provider-family-aws`, `provider-aws-iam`, and `provider-aws-eks` (provided by appmod-blueprints or installed separately).

## Deployment via appmod-blueprints

When deployed through the [appmod-blueprints](https://github.com/aws-samples/appmod-blueprints) platform, set `agent_platform: true` in `enabled-addons.yaml`. The appmod-blueprints bootstrap chart handles everything — see `gitops/AGENT-PLATFORM.md` in that repo.

- Local cluster registered in ArgoCD using its EKS ARN
- `kubectl` and `aws` CLI configured
- Crossplane installed with `provider-aws-bedrockagentcore` (for AgentCore resources)

### Pod Identity (EKS Auto Mode)

LiteLLM needs Bedrock access. Create an IAM role with Pod Identity:

## How the Agent Platform Works

### Path 1: Agent A2A (direct chat, no auth for internal access)

```
┌──────────┐     ┌───────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│  Client  │────▶│  Agent Pod        │────▶│ kagent-controller│     │   LiteLLM   │────▶│ Bedrock │
│  (curl/  │ A2A │  (bedrock-asst    │     │  (session mgmt)  │     │  (proxy)    │     │  (LLM)  │
│   UI)    │     │   or k8s-ops)     │     │                  │     │             │     │         │
└──────────┘     └───────┬───────────┘     └──────────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────┘
                         │  OpenAI-compatible API                           ▲
                         └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. Client sends JSON-RPC `message/send` to the agent's Service (port 8080)
2. Agent framework calls kagent-controller to create/manage sessions
3. Agent calls LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible) which routes to Bedrock via Pod Identity
4. For tool-using agents (k8s-ops), the agent also calls `kagent-tool-server` via MCP

### Path 2: Authenticated MCP via AgentGateway + KeyCloak

```
┌──────────┐  1.Get Token  ┌──────────────┐
│  Client  │──────────────▶│  KeyCloak    │
│          │◀──────────────│  (platform   │
│          │   JWT Token   │   realm)     │
└────┬─────┘               └──────────────┘
     │
     │ 2. MCP request + JWT
     ▼
```

# Open Agentic Platform on Amazon EKS

A production-ready AI agent platform built on Amazon EKS, featuring KAgent, LiteLLM gateway, Langfuse observability, AgentGateway (MCP auth), and multi-agent orchestration.

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- AWS account with Bedrock access
- [Task](https://taskfile.dev), kubectl, Helm 3.x, AWS CLI, `yq`
- Podman or Docker (for Kind-based bootstrap)

### Install

```bash
# 1. Configure
cp config.yaml config.local.yaml
# Edit config.local.yaml with your values

# 2. Install everything (platform + agentic components)
task install
```

That's it. The installer provisions an EKS hub cluster, deploys the base platform (ArgoCD, Crossplane, observability), then layers on the agentic components.

### Configuration

Edit `config.local.yaml`:

| Section | Key Fields | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| `platform` | `repo`, `ref` | Base platform repo and version tag |
| `aws` | `region`, `accountId`, `profile` | AWS settings |
| `hub` | `clusterName`, `kubernetesVersion` | Hub cluster config |
| `domain` | | Ingress domain (must have ACM cert + Route53 zone) |
| `identityCenter` | `instanceArn`, `region`, `adminGroupId` | SSO for ArgoCD |
| `agenticRepo` | `url`, `revision`, `basepath` | This repo's git coordinates (for ArgoCD) |
| `components` | `kagent`, `litellm`, `langfuse`, etc. | Toggle agentic components |
| `spokes` | | Optional spoke clusters (see below) |

### Spoke Clusters

Add spoke clusters for workload environments:

```yaml
spokes:
  dev:
    region: us-west-2
    kubernetesVersion: "1.35"
    vpcCidr: "10.1.0.0/16"
    autoMode: true
  prod:
    region: us-west-2
    kubernetesVersion: "1.35"
    vpcCidr: "10.2.0.0/16"
    autoMode: true
```

Spokes are provisioned via Crossplane from the hub. Agentic components deploy to all clusters automatically.

## Available Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `task install` | Full install (platform + spokes + agentic) |
| `task platform:install` | Provision base EKS platform only |
| `task spokes:install` | Provision spoke clusters only |
| `task spokes:status` | Check spoke provisioning progress |
| `task agentic:install` | Deploy agentic components only |
| `task status` | Show ArgoCD application status |
| `task upgrade` | Upgrade everything |
| `task destroy` | Remove agentic components (keeps base platform) |
| `task spokes:destroy` | Delete spoke clusters |

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  open-agentic-platform (this repo)                      │
│  config.local.yaml → task install                       │
└────────────┬────────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
             │                            │
    ┌────────▼────────┐         ┌────────▼────────┐
    │ appmod-blueprints│         │ ArgoCD Application│
    │ (base platform) │         │ (agentic addons)  │
    │ read-only clone │         │ points to this repo│
    └────────┬────────┘         └────────┬──────────┘
             │                            │
             ▼                            ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │              EKS Hub Cluster                     │
    │  ArgoCD ─── watches both repos (read-only)      │
    │  Crossplane ─── provisions spoke clusters       │
    │                                                  │
    │  Agentic: KAgent, LiteLLM, Langfuse, Jaeger,   │
    │           AgentGateway, Bifrost, AgentCore      │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **KAgent** | Kubernetes-native AI agent operator |
| **LiteLLM** | LLM gateway with rate limiting, caching, fallbacks |
| **Langfuse** | LLM observability — traces, costs, analytics |
| **Jaeger** | Distributed tracing for agent interactions |
| **AgentGateway** | MCP auth gateway with Keycloak OIDC |
| **Bifrost** | AI gateway for model routing |
| **AgentCore** | Crossplane compositions for Bedrock AgentCore |

## Workshop

The `workshop/` directory contains hands-on examples:

| Module | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `00-initial-setup` | Bedrock + LiteLLM configuration |
| `01-first-agent` | Basic KAgent with Bedrock |
| `02-k8s-ops-agent` | Kubernetes operations agent |
| `03-multi-tool-agent` | Agent with MCP tool servers |
| `04-multi-agents` | Financial services multi-agent system |
| `05-observability` | Monitoring and tracing setup |

## Resources

- [KAgent](https://kagent.dev)
- [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai)
- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/docs)
- [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock)
- [appmod-blueprints](https://github.com/aws-samples/appmod-blueprints) (base platform)
