# Agentic Platform

GitOps-managed deployment of the agentic AI infrastructure on EKS, including [AgentGateway](https://agentgateway.dev) (Gateway API for AI agents/MCP servers), a Bedrock AI backend, and a LiteLLM proxy for centralized LLM access.

## Architecture

```
gitops/agentic/
└── addons/
    ├── default/
    │   └── addons.yaml                    # Addon definitions for application-sets chart
    └── charts/
        └── agentgateway/
            ├── Chart.yaml                 # Wrapper chart (depends on oci://cr.agentgateway.dev/charts/agentgateway)
            ├── values.yaml                # Default values
            └── templates/
                ├── gateway.yaml           # Gateway API Gateway resource
                ├── bedrock-backend.yaml   # AgentgatewayBackend + HTTPRoute for Bedrock
                └── litellm.yaml           # LiteLLM proxy (Deployment, ConfigMap, Service)

gitops/fleet/bootstrap/
└── agentic-addons.yaml                    # ArgoCD ApplicationSet (entry point)
```

## What Gets Deployed

| Component | Description |
|---|---|
| AgentGateway controller | Helm chart `oci://cr.agentgateway.dev/charts/agentgateway:v2.2.1` — manages GatewayClass, proxy deployments |
| Gateway proxy | Auto-provisioned by the controller when the Gateway resource is created; exposes a LoadBalancer |
| Bedrock backend | `AgentgatewayBackend` CR pointing to Claude Sonnet on Bedrock, with an HTTPRoute |
| LiteLLM proxy | OpenAI-compatible proxy that routes to Bedrock via pod identity; used by agents as their LLM endpoint |

## Deployment

### Automatic (Recommended)

Add `enable_agentgateway: true` to the hub cluster's addons in `platform/infra/terraform/hub-config.yaml`:

```yaml
clusters:
  hub:
    addons:
      # ... existing addons ...
      enable_agentgateway: true
```

Then run the standard Terraform apply. The gitops-bridge module propagates this label to the ArgoCD cluster secret, which triggers the `agentic-addons` ApplicationSet in `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agentic-addons.yaml`. ArgoCD then deploys the agentgateway chart into the `agentgateway-system` namespace.

### Manual

If the cluster is already running and you just want to enable it without a Terraform run, add the label to the ArgoCD cluster secret directly:

```bash
kubectl label secret -n argocd -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster \
  enable_agentgateway=true --overwrite
```

ArgoCD will pick up the label change and deploy automatically.

## How the GitOps Flow Works

```
hub-config.yaml                          # 1. enable_agentgateway: true
  → Terraform (gitops-bridge)            # 2. Sets label on ArgoCD cluster secret
    → fleet/bootstrap/agentic-addons.yaml  # 3. ApplicationSet matches the label
      → agentic/addons/default/addons.yaml # 4. Addon config fed to application-sets chart
        → agentic/addons/charts/agentgateway/ # 5. Helm chart deployed to cluster
```

The `agentic-addons.yaml` ApplicationSet lives in `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/`, which is auto-synced by the top-level fleet bootstrap. It only activates when the cluster secret has `enable_agentgateway: "true"`.

## Configuration

Override values per-environment by creating additional value files:

```
gitops/agentic/addons/
├── default/addons.yaml           # Base config (always applied)
├── environments/
│   └── control-plane/addons.yaml # Environment overrides (optional)
└── clusters/
    └── hub/addons.yaml           # Cluster-specific overrides (optional)
```

### Key Values

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bedrockBackend.model` | `us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0` | Bedrock model ID |
| `bedrockBackend.region` | `us-west-2` (from cluster annotation) | AWS region for Bedrock |
| `litellm.masterKey` | `sk-1234` | LiteLLM API key (override in production) |
| `litellm.models` | Claude Sonnet via Bedrock | LLM model routing config |
| `gateway.listeners` | HTTP on port 80, all namespaces | Gateway listener config |

## Accessing the Gateway

```bash

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

# OAM Components for Agents and MCP Servers

This directory contains OAM (Open Application Model) component definitions and examples for deploying AI agents and MCP servers with Argo Rollouts on Kubernetes.

For architectural decisions and rationale, see **[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)**.

## Components

| Component | File | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `agent` | `agent.cue` | A2A agent with blue-green deployment and agentgateway registration |
| `mcp-server` | `mcp-server.cue` | MCP server with blue-green deployment, agentgateway backend, and tool-level auth |

## Files

### Agent Component
- `agent.cue` - Agent ComponentDefinition (CUE format)
- `agent-crd.yaml` - Agent ComponentDefinition wrapped for KubeVela registration
- `example-agent-simple.yaml` - Basic agent example
- `example-agent-with-mcp.yaml` - Agent with MCP tool integration
- `example-agent-minimal.yaml` - Minimal agent example
- `kagent-rollout-component.yaml` - Legacy ComponentDefinition with canary/blue-green support

### MCP Server Component
- `mcp-server.cue` - MCP server ComponentDefinition (CUE format)
- `example-mcp-local.yaml` - Example: deploy mcp-time-server via KubeVela

### Infrastructure
- `agentgateway-backend.yaml` - AgentGateway backend configuration for Bedrock
- `agentgateway-httproute.yaml` - HTTP routing configuration
- `register-agent-with-gateway.yaml` - Examples for registering agents with AgentGateway
- `appmod-service.cue` - Full-featured service ComponentDefinition with canary/blue-green support
- `litellm-deployment.yaml` - LiteLLM proxy deployment
- `kgateway-session-affinity.yaml` - Session affinity configuration

### Utilities
- `generate-component-from-cue.sh` - Helper script to generate CRD from CUE files
- `vela-cue-commands.md` - Documentation for vela CLI commands

## Important Note About Images

The example files use `tiangolo/uvicorn-gunicorn-fastapi:python3.11` as a placeholder image for testing the Argo Rollouts mechanism. This is NOT a Strands agent image and will not provide actual agent functionality.

To use real Strands agents, you must build and push your own images following the instructions below.

## Prerequisites

1. Kubernetes cluster with:
   - KubeVela installed
   - Argo Rollouts installed
   - AWS Load Balancer Controller (for ALB traffic routing)

2. AWS resources:
   - Amazon Bedrock access with Claude models enabled
   - ECR repository for your Strands agent images
   - IAM roles/service accounts for pod identity

## Building a Strands Agent Image

You can build a Strands agent image using the provided application in `applications/strands/`:

```bash
# Navigate to the Strands application directory
cd applications/strands

# Build for AMD64 (compatible with AWS EKS)
./build.sh

# Or use Podman
./build-podman.sh

# Push to ECR
./build.sh push
# Or with Podman
./build-podman.sh push
```

The build scripts automatically:
- Build for AMD64 architecture
- Detect AWS account ID and region
- Create ECR repository if needed
- Tag and push to ECR

See `applications/strands/README.md` for detailed instructions.

Alternatively, follow the [official Strands EKS deployment guide](https://strandsagents.com/latest/documentation/docs/examples/deploy_to_eks/).

## Setting up Pod Identity for Bedrock

### Option 1: Using LLM Gateway (Recommended)

The LLM Gateway (LiteLLM proxy) provides centralized LLM access with pod identity authentication. The gateway handles authentication to Bedrock, so individual agents don't need AWS credentials.

Benefits:
- No AWS credentials needed in agent pods
- Centralized access control and monitoring
- Simplified agent deployment
- Support for multiple LLM providers

The agent.cue ComponentDefinition uses LLM Gateway by default:

=== platform/oam/DESIGN.md preview ===
# OAM Component Design Decisions

This document captures architectural and design decisions for the KubeVela OAM components in this platform: **agent** (A2A) and **mcp-server** (MCP).

---

## Shared Decisions (Both Components)

### Blue-Green Deployment via Argo Rollouts

Both components use Argo Rollouts with blue-green strategy as the primary workload resource (not Deployment).

**How it works**:
- The Rollout creates two Services: `<name>-stable` (active) and `<name>-preview`.
- On image update, the new version deploys to preview. After promotion, it becomes stable.
- Argo Rollouts manages which ReplicaSet backs which service via selector injection.
- Default: auto-promotion enabled, 10s promotion delay, 30s scale-down delay.

**Gateway API plugin**: kgateway/agentgateway supports the Argo Rollouts Gateway API traffic router plugin (`argoproj-labs/gatewayAPI`) for canary with traffic splitting. For blue-green, the standard service selector approach works without the plugin since backends always point to the stable service.

**Reference**: [kgateway Argo Rollouts integration](https://kgateway.dev/docs/envoy/main/integrations/argo)

### KubeVela OAM Pattern

Both components follow the same structure:
- `.cue` file defines the component template with parameters
- A `ComponentDefinition` YAML wraps the CUE template for registration with KubeVela
- An `Application` YAML instantiates the component with specific properties

### Gateway Registration

Both components optionally register with agentgateway via HTTPRoute (`registerWithGateway: true` by default). The route attaches to the `agentgateway-proxy` Gateway in `agentgateway-system`.

### Service Port Convention

Services expose port 80 externally, mapping to the container's application port. This matches agentgateway documentation conventions and simplifies backend configuration.

---

## Agent Component (`agent.cue`)

The `agent` component deploys A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol agents.

### Generated Resources

1. **Argo Rollout** — blue-green deployment
2. **Stable Service** — `appProtocol: kgateway.dev/a2a`, port 8083
3. **Preview Service** — blue-green preview
4. **Agent Card ConfigMap** — metadata for agent discovery
5. **HTTPRoute** — routes `/<name>` to stable service (optional)

### LLM Access via Gateway (Not Direct Bedrock)

**Decision**: Agents access LLMs through a centralized LiteLLM proxy gateway, not directly via AWS Bedrock credentials.

**Why**:
- No AWS credentials needed in agent pods
- Centralized access control, monitoring, and cost tracking
- Support for multiple LLM providers behind a single endpoint
- Simplified agent deployment

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: cluster-addons
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"
spec:
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: false
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions:
    - missingkey=error
  generators:
    - clusters:
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            fleet_member: control-plane
        values:
          addonChart: application-sets
  template:
    metadata:
      name: cluster-addons
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - ref: values
          repoURL: '{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_url}}'
          targetRevision: '{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_revision}}'
        - repoURL: '{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_url}}'
          path: '{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_basepath}}charts/{{.values.addonChart}}'
          targetRevision: '{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_revision}}'
          helm:
            ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
            valueFiles:
              - $values/{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_basepath}}bootstrap/default/addons.yaml
              - $values/{{.metadata.annotations.addons_repo_basepath}}environments/{{ .metadata.labels.environment }}/addons.yaml
      destination:
        namespace: argocd
        name: '{{.name}}'
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          selfHeal: true
          allowEmpty: true
          prune: true
        retry:
          limit: 100
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: agent-platform-addons
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  sources:
    - ref: values
      repoURL: "${REPO_URL}"
      targetRevision: "${REVISION}"
    - repoURL: "${REPO_URL}"
      path: "${BASEPATH}charts/application-sets"
      targetRevision: "${REVISION}"
      helm:
        releaseName: agent-platform-addons
        ignoreMissingValueFiles: true
        valueFiles:
          - "$values/${BASEPATH}bootstrap/default/addons.yaml"
          - "$values/${BASEPATH}environments/control-plane/addons.yaml"
        valuesObject:
          useSelectors: false
          globalSelectors:
            enable_agent_platform: "true"
          repoURLGit: "${REPO_URL}"
          repoURLGitRevision: "${REVISION}"
          repoURLGitBasePath: "${BASEPATH}"
  destination:
    namespace: argocd
    name: ${HUB_CLUSTER_NAME}
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      selfHeal: true
      allowEmpty: true
      prune: true
    retry:
      limit: 100
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true
      - ServerSideApply=true

{{- $values := .Values }}
{{- $syncPolicy := .Values.syncPolicy -}}
{{- $syncPolicyAppSet := .Values.syncPolicyAppSet -}}
{{- $repoURLGit := .Values.repoURLGit -}}
{{- $repoURLGitRevision := .Values.repoURLGitRevision -}}
{{- $repoURLGitBasePath := .Values.repoURLGitBasePath -}}
{{- $valueFiles := .Values.valueFiles -}}
{{- $valuesFilePrefix := .Values.valuesFilePrefix -}}
{{- $useValuesFilePrefix := (default false .Values.useValuesFilePrefix) -}}
{{- $useSelectors := .Values.useSelectors -}}
{{- $globalSelectors := .Values.globalSelectors -}}

{{- range $chartName, $chartConfig := .Values }}
{{- if and (kindIs "map" $chartConfig) (hasKey $chartConfig "enabled") }}
{{- if eq (toString $chartConfig.enabled) "true" }}
{{- $nameNormalize := printf "%s" $chartName | replace "_" "-" | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" -}}
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: {{ $nameNormalize }}
  namespace: {{ default "argocd" $values.namespace }}
  annotations:
    {{- include "application-sets.annotations" $ | nindent 4 }}
    {{- if $chartConfig.annotationsAppSet }}{{- toYaml $chartConfig.annotationsAppSet | nindent 4 }}{{- end }}
  labels:
    {{- include "application-sets.labels" $ | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions:
    - missingkey=error
  {{- if $chartConfig.syncPolicyAppSet }}
  syncPolicy:
  {{- toYaml $chartConfig.syncPolicyAppSet | nindent 4 }}
  {{- else }}
  syncPolicy:
  {{- toYaml $syncPolicyAppSet | nindent 4 }}
  {{- end }}
  generators:
    - clusters:
        selector:
          matchLabels:
            argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster
            {{- if $globalSelectors }}
            {{- toYaml $globalSelectors | nindent 12 }}
            {{- end }}
          {{- if and $chartConfig.selector $useSelectors }}
          {{- toYaml $chartConfig.selector | nindent 10 }}
          {{- end }}
        {{- if not $chartConfig.path }}
        values:
          addonChart: {{ $chartConfig.chartName | default $nameNormalize | quote }}
          {{- if $chartConfig.defaultVersion }}
          addonChartVersion: {{ $chartConfig.defaultVersion | quote }}
          {{- end }}
          {{- if $chartConfig.chartRepository }}
          addonChartRepository: {{ $chartConfig.chartRepository | quote }}
          {{- end }}
          {{- if $chartConfig.chartNamespace }}
          addonChartRepositoryNamespace: {{ $chartConfig.chartNamespace | quote }}
          chart: {{ printf "%s/%s" $chartConfig.chartNamespace ($chartConfig.chartName | default $nameNormalize) | quote }}

I see that the OAP target's addon configuration is fundamentally different from the appmod version—it's a streamlined set of agentic-platform addons without a `kubevela:` entry. I need to add both the `kubevela:` and `mcp-gateway-operator:` entries to OAP's `bootstrap/default/addons.yaml`.

The `agentgateway` addon already exists in OAP but uses the upstream OCI chart directly as a controller-only deployment, whereas the source has a wrapper chart that bundles the controller with Gateway resources, bedrock backend, and litellm. Since OAP separates these concerns—using `agentgateway-crds` for CRDs, `agentgateway` for the controller, and `agent-gateway` for platform resources—I shouldn't migrate the source's wrapper chart wholesale. Instead, I'll need to fold the bedrock-backend and litellm pieces into the `agent-gateway` chart or keep them as separate addons, since litellm is already configured as its own addon in the target.

I also noticed that the tracked `.venv` and `__pycache__` files in `applications/strands/` are accidents based on the `.gitignore` rules, so those shouldn't migrate either.

Before proceeding with the full migration plan, I should clarify some architectural decisions with the user rather than making them unilaterally.

content.data:
I have a complete picture now. Let me lay out what I found, and then ask the key decision questions before staging anything.

## Migration scope (source → target)

### Source: `appmod-blueprints` `feature/oam-for-agents`

OAM-for-agents work is concentrated in 5 areas:

| Source path | Files | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `platform/oam/definitions/{components,configs}/*.cue` | 14 | CUE source for ComponentDefinitions (agent, mcp-server, agentcore-memory, dynamodb, rds, s3, etc.) |
| `platform/oam/examples/*.yaml` + `{README,DESIGN,TODO}.md` + `generate.sh` | 15 | Examples, docs, codegen script |
| `gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/templates/components/*.yaml` (+ configs) | 14 | Generated YAML wrappers for KubeVela registration |
| `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/agentgateway/` (wrapper chart) | 6 | Wraps `oci://cr.agentgateway.dev/charts/agentgateway:v2.2.1` + adds Gateway, bedrock-backend, litellm |
| `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/mcp-gateway-operator/` | 12 | Operator chart with AgentCore gateway + OAuth2 + pod identity |
| `gitops/agentic/{README.md, addons/default/addons.yaml}` | 2 | Addon registration for the parallel `agentic` hierarchy |
| `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agentic-addons.yaml` | 1 | Standalone ApplicationSet that loads `gitops/agentic/...` |
| `applications/strands/` (clean) | 29 | Strands sample agent app |
| `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` | partial diff | Adds `platformEnv`/`environment.name` to existing `kubevela`/`crossplane-aws` entries |

### Junk to drop from migration

- `applications/strands/.venv/*` and `applications/strands/app/__pycache__/*` (the source's own `.gitignore` excludes these — they were tracked by accident, ~hundreds of files of noise)
- `applications/dotnet/src/.../obj/*` (.NET build artifacts; nothing to do with OAM)
- `hack/.zsh_history`, `hack/.bashrc.d/*`, `.kiro/agents/...` (local IDE state)
- All version **downgrades** in `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` (argocd 9.5.12→9.4.9, cert-manager 1.20.2→1.19.4, crossplane 2.2.1→2.2.0, mlflow 1.8.1→1.7.2, etc. — these look like accidental conflict-resolution regressions and the target's version of the file is a curated agentic-platform-only one anyway)
- `gitops/fleet/members/fleet-spoke-{dev,prod}/values.yaml` (deletions of files that don't exist in target — target uses `spoke-{dev,prod}/` naming)

### Target: `open-agentic-platform` `feature/oam-for-agents`

What's already there that affects mapping:

- `gitops/addons/charts/agent-gateway/` — **platform-resources chart** (Gateway, HTTPRoute, Backend, JWT/MCP policies, Ingress) tied to KeyCloak. Different scope from source's `agentgateway/` wrapper.
- `gitops/addons/charts/litellm/` — already a standalone chart (source bundles litellm inside its agentgateway wrapper)
- `gitops/addons/charts/{kagent,kagent-setup,kagent-monitoring,langfuse,otel-collector,bifrost,crossplane-agentcore,gateway-api-crds,application-sets}/` — full agentic stack
- `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` — **curated 358-line agentic-only file** with addon defs for `agentgateway` (using the OCI chart directly, no wrapper), `agent-gateway` (the resources chart), `agentgateway-crds`, etc. **No `kubevela:` entry yet, no `mcp-gateway-operator:` entry yet.**
- `gitops/addons/environments/control-plane/addons.yaml` — already lists `agentgateway: true` and `agent-gateway: true`. No `kubevela`, no `mcp-gateway-operator`.
- `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/{addons,agent-platform-app}.yaml` — single ApplicationSet/Application loading the bootstrap+env addons. **No parallel `agentic-addons.yaml` ApplicationSet** (target uses the unified one).
- No `platform/oam/`, no `applications/strands/`, no `gitops/agentic/`, no `docs/`.

## Architectural differences worth flagging

**The source uses a parallel `gitops/agentic/` hierarchy with its own ApplicationSet.** The target uses a single `gitops/addons/` hierarchy and a single fleet bootstrap. To fit the target's pattern cleanly:

- `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/X/` → flatten to `gitops/addons/charts/X/`
- `gitops/agentic/addons/default/addons.yaml` → merge entries into `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml`
- `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agentic-addons.yaml` → **drop** (target's existing `bootstrap/addons.yaml` already covers this)

**The source's `agentgateway/` wrapper chart bundles three things**: controller subchart, Gateway+bedrock-backend, litellm. The target separates these:
- controller → `agentgateway/` addon (using OCI chart directly, no wrapper) **already in target**
- Gateway + backends → `agent-gateway/` chart **already in target** (with KeyCloak JWT auth as bonus)
- litellm → `litellm/` chart **already in target**

So the source's wrapper chart largely **duplicates** existing target functionality. The bedrock-backend `AgentgatewayBackend` + HTTPRoute is the only new bit, and it would naturally live as a new template in the existing `agent-gateway/` chart, gated by a value flag.

---

## Decision points — please answer before I stage anything

**1. Scope of migration: docs+CUE only, or full agentic addon stack?**

   Three options:
   - **(a) Minimal**: Only the OAM artifacts proper — `platform/oam/` (CUE + examples + docs) + `gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/templates/components/` (generated YAML) + the kubevela entry in bootstrap addons. Skip `gitops/agentic/`, skip strands app, skip the wrapper chart.
   - **(b) OAM + new operator**: Above + `mcp-gateway-operator/` (genuinely new in target). Skip the agentgateway wrapper (target already has it differently), skip strands.
   - **(c) Full**: Everything, including strands app and reconciling the agentgateway wrapper with the target's split (means you'd fold bedrock-backend into `agent-gateway/`, drop the wrapper's litellm, merge the `agentic/addons/default/addons.yaml` into the target's bootstrap addons).

   My recommendation: **(b)** for the PR. It's clean, doesn't fight the target's existing split, and the strands app can come later as its own PR. But you may have a different preference.

**2. Should generated YAML (`gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/templates/components/*.yaml`) be committed, or regenerated at the target via `generate.sh`?**

   - **Commit**: target only needs `helm install` to work — no CUE toolchain required at deploy time.
   - **Regenerate**: cleaner source-of-truth; the .cue files are the only authoritative artifact.
   
   The source repo commits both. I'd commit both for consistency with how the source treats them. Confirm or override.

**3. `agentgateway` wrapper chart from source — what to do with its three pieces?**

   - Bedrock backend YAML (`bedrock-backend.yaml`): fold into target's `agent-gateway/` chart as a new template (`bedrock-backend.yaml`), gated by `bedrockBackend.enabled`?
   - Gateway YAML (`gateway.yaml`): target's `agent-gateway/` already has `gateway.yaml`. Skip the source's, OR diff and merge any improvements?
   - LiteLLM YAML (`litellm.yaml`): drop — target has its own `litellm/` chart already.

   Or, alternatively, keep the source's wrapper as a **separate** chart (`gitops/addons/charts/agentgateway-bundle/` or similar) and let the target user enable either the unbundled stack or the bundle. Less clean but preserves the source's bundling intent.

**4. Where do `platform/oam/{README,DESIGN,TODO}.md` go?**

   - **Co-located** at `platform/oam/` (alongside the CUE) — what the source does.
   - **Centralized** at `docs/oam/` — would create a `docs/` dir at the OAP root.

   I'd default to co-located since the OAP repo currently has no `docs/` and these docs are tightly coupled to the CUE files.

**5. Strands app destination if migrating (full-scope option)**

   - `applications/strands/` (top-level — mirrors source layout)
   - `workshop/06-strands-app/` (aligns with existing `01-first-agent`, `03-multi-tool-agent` workshop modules)
   
   These have different audiences — `applications/` is a build-and-deploy artifact, `workshop/` is a learning module. If migrating, my recommendation is `applications/strands/` since it has a Dockerfile + tests, not a workshop README walkthrough. But if your aim is to also use it as a workshop step, `workshop/` is right.

**6. Source-branch hygiene: do you want me to also cherry-pick out the unrelated stuff (CVE bumps in commits 222fa764, ec872023) so they don't pollute the source branch later?**

   Out of scope for the OAM-migration PR but worth noting — the source branch tip mixes OAM work with CVE fixes for haproxy/strands. I won't touch it unless asked.

**7. The diff to `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` (in source)**

   Two real additions worth migrating:
   - `kubevela:` entry now has `platformEnv: { envName, clusterName, region }` valuesObject
   - `crossplane-aws:` entry now has `environment.name` valuesObject
   
   Should these land in the target's `bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` too? The target file is a **different curated subset** — its kubevela section doesn't even exist yet (need to add fresh from source), and crossplane-aws also doesn't exist (only `crossplane-agentcore` does). So we'd be **adding** kubevela and possibly leaving crossplane-aws alone.

---

Once you answer these, I'll stage the changes in `/Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform` on `feature/oam-for-agents` (no commit), and report back exactly what got staged so you can review before any commit.

Looking at the KubeVela chart structure, I can see it's a Helm chart with vela-core as a dependency at version 1.10.7, which is vendored locally. The chart includes templates for both platform and agentic components, along with configuration files for the platform environment.

The key insight is that the traits and configs like ingress are platform concerns that should remain in appmod-blueprints, while the agentic ComponentDefinitions need a different approach. Since the user clarified that KubeVela itself comes from the platform, I shouldn't migrate the entire kubevela chart to OAP. Instead, the agentic ComponentDefinitions should be provisioned separately as Custom Resources to the existing KubeVela installation. I'm considering either creating a dedicated Helm chart in OAP specifically for the agentic components, or vendoring the YAMLs directly under the platform directory. The chart would contain templates for the three ComponentDefinition YAMLs, and I need to decide whether to register this as a Helm chart addon in OAP's bootstrap configuration or keep the bare YAMLs applied separately. The user clarified that the kubevela bootstrap entries are handled by the feature/agent-platform branch, so I'm focusing on just registering the agentic ComponentDefinitions themselves as an addon. Option A feels right — staging the chart in `gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components/` mirrors OAP's existing patterns and lets it plug into addon registration later once feature/agent-platform lands. For the gateway, the target's concrete single-listener approach is fine and doesn't need anything from the source. The strands-agent-base app is a fresh sample moving to `applications/strands-agent-base/`, and since the source versions are actually stale compared to the target, there are no CVE bumps to backport — just need to note that the new app uses Python 3.13.

Now I'm checking what the source's component YAML format looks like so I can properly migrate the three agentic components. For the docs, DESIGN.md is all agent and MCP focused so it moves to OAP, but TODO.md is about platform-env config which is a generic platform concern — that stays in appmod. README needs to be trimmed to agentic-only content.

For the OAP structure, I'm planning to create the component definitions in CUE format, the generate script, and then populate the examples directory with all the agent deployment scenarios, MCP configurations, and gateway-related examples. I'll skip litellm-deployment since the user said to ignore it.

I also need to include the Helm chart structure for the OAM agent components with templated YAML files, plus the full strands-agent-base application directory. Before I proceed with staging everything, let me quickly check if that kgateway-session-affinity example is actually agentic or if it should be skipped.

## Staging complete — summary

**50 files staged** on `feature/oam-for-agents` in `/Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform`. **Nothing committed** per your instruction.

### What got staged

| Path | Files | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `platform/oam/` | 17 | 3 CUE files (agent, mcp-server, agentcore-memory), `generate.sh`, README.md, DESIGN.md, 11 examples |
| `gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components/` | 4 | New thin Helm chart: Chart.yaml + 3 ComponentDefinition templates |
| `applications/strands-agent-base/` | 29 | Renamed copy of source's `applications/strands/` (clean, no `.venv`/`__pycache__`) |

All files copied from source's HEAD (`222fa764` on `feature/oam-for-agents`) via `git archive | tar` for atomicity.

### What was deliberately NOT migrated (and why)

| Skipped | Reason |
|---|---|
| `platform/oam/TODO.md` | Platform concern (platform-env config, generic to any cluster) — stays in appmod |
| `platform/oam/examples/litellm-deployment.yaml` | You said ignore litellm |
| Platform CUE: `appmod-service`, `dp-service-account`, `dynamodb-*`, `rds-*`, `s3-*`, `external-database-secret`, `platform-env` (config) | Platform concerns — stay in appmod |
| `gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/` (the source's chart) | KubeVela is provisioned by the platform; OAP shouldn't ship vela-core |
| `gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/templates/traits/{ingress,component-policy,path-based-ingress}.yaml` | Platform traits (especially `ingress`) — stay in appmod |
| `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/agentgateway/` (wrapper chart) | Target already separates these: `agentgateway/` controller + `agent-gateway/` resources + `litellm/` chart. Wrapper would duplicate. |
| `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/mcp-gateway-operator/` | Out of scope per your decision (point 1) |
| `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agentic-addons.yaml` | Target's existing fleet bootstrap already covers it |
| Source's bootstrap/default/addons.yaml diff | Mostly version downgrades (regressions); kubevela/crossplane-aws additions are platform's job |
| `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.NET obj/` build artifacts | Junk |

### Notable findings during analysis

- **Gateway YAML comparison** (you asked me to check): source's `gitops/agentic/addons/charts/agentgateway/templates/gateway.yaml` is essentially the same shape as target's `gitops/addons/charts/agent-gateway/templates/gateway.yaml`. The source uses `.Values.gateway.listeners` for flexibility; target hardcodes a single HTTP listener on `gatewayPort: 8080`. **Nothing meaningful to carry over** — both produce a single-listener `agentgateway-proxy` Gateway in `agentgateway-system`.

- **Version comparison for CVE bumps** (your point 6): The source's `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` diff against main shows **only downgrades** (argocd 9.5.12→9.4.9, cert-manager v1.20.2→v1.19.4, crossplane 2.2.1→2.2.0, mlflow 1.8.1→1.7.2, etc.) — these look like accidental conflict-resolution regressions. Source is **behind** target on every shared addon. **Nothing to cherry-pick** — target already has the better versions, or has different/curated entries entirely.

- **Strands Dockerfile**: source uses `python:3.13-slim-bookworm` with `apt-get upgrade` for CVE patching. This is a fresh new app in OAP, no existing version to compare against. The Dockerfile already has the CVE-fix layer baked in.

### Two unresolved items worth flagging

**1. The new chart isn't registered as an addon.** I did not modify `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` to add an `oam-agent-components:` entry, since you said feature/agent-platform handles addon registration. When that branch lands and you wire it in, the entry would look something like:

```yaml
oam-agent-components:
  enabled: false
  namespace: vela-system
  defaultVersion: '0.1.0'
  path: 'gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components'
  annotationsAppSet:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '5'   # after kubevela (must be installed first)
  selector:
    matchExpressions:
      - key: enable_oam_agent_components
        operator: In
        values: ['true']
```

Just want you aware that without this entry, the chart sits unused.

**2. The README and DESIGN docs reference the source paths verbatim.** For example, `platform/oam/README.md` mentions `applications/strands/` (no `-agent-base` suffix), and DESIGN.md references components like `appmod-service.cue` that are no longer present in OAP. I left them as-is since you said *"only stage change now, do not commit"* — you may want to clean these references in a follow-up edit before committing, or I can do it on request.

When you're ready, I can:

- Add the `oam-agent-components` addon entry to `bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` (you may prefer to wait for feature/agent-platform to merge first)
- Stage corresponding edits in the source appmod repo (delete the now-migrated files there) — only on your go-ahead

input.title: feat(oam): migrate agentic OAM components from appmod-blueprints
input.head: feature/oam-for-agents
input.body:
## Summary

Moves the OAM artifacts that are specific to the agentic platform out of `appmod-blueprints` and into this repo, leaving generic platform components (appmod-service, dp-service-account, dynamodb-*, rds-*, s3-*, ingress trait, platform-env config) where they belong. **KubeVela itself continues to be provisioned by the platform** — this PR ships only the agentic ComponentDefinitions and supporting artifacts.

## What changed

| Path | Files | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `platform/oam/` | 17 | CUE sources for `agent`, `mcp-server`, `agentcore-memory` ComponentDefinitions, plus `generate.sh`, README, DESIGN, and 11 examples |
| `gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components/` | 4 | Thin Helm chart packaging the three ComponentDefinition manifests for cluster registration |
| `applications/strands-agent-base/` | 29 | Reference Strands agent app (Dockerfile, build scripts, unit + integration tests, A2A and gateway fixtures) |

**Total: 50 files, +5920 lines, no deletions.**

## Migration scope rationale

This PR was deliberately scoped to **agentic-only** artifacts. Things explicitly left in `appmod-blueprints`:

- Generic platform CUE: `appmod-service`, `dp-service-account`, `dynamodb-ack`, `dynamodb-table`, `rds-cluster`, `rds-cluster-mysql`, `s3-bucket`, `s3-bucket-ack`, `external-database-secret`, `platform-env` (config)
- Generic platform traits: `ingress`, `path-based-ingress`, `component-policy`
- KubeVela helm chart itself (`gitops/addons/charts/kubevela/`) — platform installs vela-core
- TODO.md (about platform-env config — generic concern)

Things deliberately not migrated even though they exist on the source branch:

- **`mcp-gateway-operator` chart** — out of scope per current iteration
- **`agentgateway` wrapper chart** — duplicates this repo's existing split (`agentgateway/` controller + `agent-gateway/` resources + `litellm/` chart). Bedrock-backend and litellm pieces from the wrapper are redundant here.
- **`gitops/agentic/` parallel hierarchy + `agentic-addons.yaml` ApplicationSet** — this repo uses a single unified addon hierarchy
- **Source's bootstrap `addons.yaml` diff** — mostly version regressions (argocd 9.5.12→9.4.9, cert-manager v1.20.2→v1.19.4, crossplane 2.2.1→2.2.0, mlflow 1.8.1→1.7.2, etc.); this repo is ahead on all shared addon versions

## Open items (intentional follow-ups, not blockers)

1. **Addon registration**: `oam-agent-components` chart is **not yet wired** into `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml`. Waiting on the platform-side KubeVela provisioning work in `feature/agent-platform` to land first. Suggested entry once ready:

   ```yaml
   oam-agent-components:
     enabled: false
     namespace: vela-system
     defaultVersion: '0.1.0'
     path: 'gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components'
     annotationsAppSet:
       argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '5'   # after kubevela
     selector:
       matchExpressions:
         - key: enable_oam_agent_components
           operator: In
           values: ['true']
   ```

2. **Doc references not yet updated**: `platform/oam/README.md` still references `applications/strands/` (path renamed to `strands-agent-base/` in this PR) and DESIGN.md mentions platform components like `appmod-service.cue` that aren't in this repo. These will be cleaned in a follow-up commit on this branch before merging.

3. **Source-branch cleanup**: corresponding deletions in `appmod-blueprints` (removing the migrated agentic files) will land in a separate PR there.

## Tested

- [x] `git archive | tar` faithful copy verified — line counts match source for all 3 generated ComponentDefinition YAMLs (agent.yaml 296L, mcp-server.yaml 265L, agentcore-memory.yaml 85L)
- [x] No `.venv` / `__pycache__` / build artifacts leaked into the strands-agent-base copy
- [x] Nothing staged outside the three target directories
- [ ] `helm template gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components/` smoke test
- [ ] End-to-end: `helm install` against a cluster with KubeVela already running → ComponentDefinitions registered → example Application deploys

## Source provenance

Branch: `feature/oam-for-agents` in `aws-samples/appmod-blueprints`
Source HEAD at migration: `222fa7648c24cdf40f97fbf12fdef14d7e83e1f8`

**No — none of them are on `main`.** All apps deployed from the `sample-open-agentic-platform` repo are pointing to `feature/refactor-agent-platform`.

### Counts

- **47 ArgoCD Applications** referencing `sample-open-agentic-platform` → all on `feature/refactor-agent-platform`
- **15 ApplicationSets** referencing the same → all on `feature/refactor-agent-platform`
- **0 references to `main`**

### What's on `feature/refactor-agent-platform`

The full agentic addon stack on hub + both spokes:

| Addon | Hub | spoke-dev | spoke-prod |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| agent-gateway, agentgateway, agentgateway-crds | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| crossplane-agentcore | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| gateway-api-crds | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| kagent, kagent-crds, kagent-setup, kagent-monitoring | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| langfuse, litellm, jaeger, otel-collector, prometheus-operator-crds, bifrost | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Plus:
- `agent-platform-addons` (the bootstrap Application that drives the ApplicationSets)
- `clusters-default`, `fleet-secret-*` (multi-cluster wiring)

### Context

`feature/refactor-agent-platform` is the branch that was merged into `main` via **PR #16** (commit `d321d08` — "Merge pull request #16 from aws-samples/feature/refactor-agent-platform"). So **right now main and that feature branch likely have the same content**, but:

- New commits to `main` won't be picked up — the apps will diverge as soon as anything lands post-merge
- The branch is still acting as a live deployment target rather than a frozen artifact
- This is exactly the situation that bites you when feature branches get rebased or deleted

### Note on `appmod-blueprints` references

Three multi-source apps also reference the platform repo as a second source (not on `main` either):

- `clusters-default`, `fleet-secret-peeks-hub`, `fleet-secret-spoke-dev`, `fleet-secret-spoke-prod` → `aws-samples/appmod-blueprints` on `feature/agent-platform-shapirov`

You didn't ask about these but flagging since they're related multi-cluster wiring.

### Recommended fix

If you want the live cluster on `main`, the branch reference in each ArgoCD `Application`/`ApplicationSet` needs to flip from `feature/refactor-agent-platform` to `main`. The source of truth for these is whatever generated them (Terraform `agent-platform-app.yaml` or the application-sets chart values). Want me to:

1. **Trace the source** that's setting `feature/refactor-agent-platform` and flip it (likely a single value in the platform Terraform or the bootstrap Application), or
2. **Just patch the live apps** in-place as a quick verification (less ideal — GitOps will revert them on next sync)?

data.text:
The user wants to test the `feature/oam-for-agents` branch on the live cluster, which is currently running `feature/refactor-agent-platform`. I need to think through the options for switching branches across the cluster infrastructure.

The key insight is that `feature/oam-for-agents` was branched from main (which already has the refactor merged in), so it contains everything the current branch has plus 50 new files for OAM support — no modifications to existing code. This means swapping branches should be functionally safe since the changes are purely additive.

I'm distinguishing between two testing scenarios: either just verifying the branch swap doesn't break anything (likely what the user means), or actually testing the OAM functionality end-to-end, which would require KubeVela to be installed and the new addon to be registered. The simpler path is probably just confirming stability after the swap, then iterating from there.

For actually making the swap, I'm weighing a few approaches: finding and updating the source-of-truth configuration (Terraform or environment variable) that currently points to the refactor branch, patching the ArgoCD Application directly for quick testing (though GitOps might revert it), spinning up a separate test cluster (overkill), or targeting just the spoke-dev environment first to validate before touching hub. The most practical move is tracing where the branch reference lives in the infrastructure-as-code and flipping it for the dev environment. The user's branch is additive-only — 50 new files in new paths, no changes to existing apps — so swapping to it should be a safe regression test. The real test has two parts: confirming existing apps stay healthy (low risk), and actually using the new OAM components (which requires KubeVela installation and registering the new chart as an addon, a separate bigger task). The cleanest approach is to flip the Terraform variable from `feature/refactor-agent-platform` to `feature/oam-for-agents`, run `terraform apply`, and let ArgoCD pick up the new revision automatically, then verify the apps remain healthy. Each spoke cluster has its own cluster secret with the `addons_repo_revision` annotation, so I can test by patching just spoke-dev's annotation to the feature branch while leaving spoke-prod unchanged — this lets me verify the changes in isolation before rolling out everywhere. The cleanest approach is to patch the cluster secret in-place for testing (which will revert if Terraform reapplies), then update the Terraform variable to make it permanent.

I found the configuration file at `/Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform/config.local.yaml` that specifies the repository URL and the feature branch being used. The Taskfile reads this configuration through `yq` and passes it to ArgoCD.

Looking at the Taskfile, I can see it exposes `AGENTIC_REPO_REVISION` sourced from the config, which gets used when creating the Application with the target revision. So the approach is straightforward: update the `agenticRepo.revision` in the config file to point to `feature/oam-for-agents`, then re-run the Taskfile task that applies the agent-platform-app Application. ArgoCD will then update the targetRevision across all 47 child Applications.

The main consideration is that since the new branch only adds 50 new files without modifying existing ones, the cluster's current apps will see identical content — so this is a low-risk additive change. The real test will be whether the new OAM functionality works once KubeVela is installed.

I'm thinking through a two-tier approach: first, a quick regression test by swapping branches and verifying all apps stay healthy, then if needed, a deeper test that involves installing KubeVela and actually deploying the new OAM components to exercise the functionality.

There's a complication though — changing config.local.yaml is a global setting that would flip the revision for spoke-dev and spoke-prod too, not just the hub. Since agent-platform-addons only lives on the hub but drives ApplicationSet templates across all clusters, there's no easy per-cluster toggle without restructuring how the revision gets injected. The practical option is a full global swap, though the risk is minimal since the new branch is purely additive. I'll recommend the global swap as the simplest path forward.

content.data:
Found the source of truth. Here's the picture and a tiered test approach:

## Source of truth (where the branch reference lives)

**`/Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform/config.local.yaml`** — line:
```yaml
agenticRepo:
  url: "https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-open-agentic-platform.git"
  revision: "feature/refactor-agent-platform"   # <-- this drives everything
```

The Taskfile reads this via `yq`, exports it as `AGENTIC_REPO_REVISION`, and substitutes it into `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agent-platform-app.yaml` (the parent Application). ArgoCD then propagates it to all 47 child Applications via the multi-source pattern. So **one config change + one task run flips everything**.

Note: cluster-secret annotations (`addons_repo_revision`) are **null** for all three clusters — the revision is **not** coming from cluster secrets, so there's no per-cluster override available without restructuring. A swap is global (hub + both spokes).

## Risk assessment

PR #18 is **additive only** — 50 new files in new paths (`platform/oam/`, `gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components/`, `applications/strands-agent-base/`). Zero edits to existing files, zero deletions. The currently-deployed addons (agentgateway, agent-gateway, kagent, langfuse, etc.) reference paths that haven't changed between `feature/refactor-agent-platform` and `feature/oam-for-agents`. So the swap should be a **functional no-op for the running cluster**. Worth verifying anyway.

## Recommended approach — tiered test

### Tier 1: Branch swap + regression test (~5 min, safe)

What it tests: does swapping the source branch break any existing apps?

```bash
cd /Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform

# 1. Edit config.local.yaml
yq -i '.agenticRepo.revision = "feature/oam-for-agents"' config.local.yaml

# 2. Re-render the agent-platform-app.yaml with the new revision
#    (the Taskfile task that bootstraps the parent app — likely 'task bootstrap'
#    or similar; let's confirm the exact task name first)
task --list-all | grep -iE "bootstrap|agent.*platform"

# 3. Re-apply only the parent Application to swap targetRevision
#    (don't run full bootstrap — too heavy)
envsubst < gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agent-platform-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# 4. Watch reconciliation
kubectl -n argocd get application -w
```

**Verify after sync settles:**
```bash
# All apps should be Healthy / Synced
kubectl -n argocd get application -o custom-columns=\
NAME:.metadata.name,SYNC:.status.sync.status,HEALTH:.status.health.status \
| grep -v "Synced.*Healthy" | head -20

# Confirm targetRevision flipped on all child apps
kubectl -n argocd get application -o json | jq -r \
  '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name)\t\(.spec.source.targetRevision // .spec.sources[0].targetRevision)"' \
  | grep -v "feature/oam-for-agents" | head -10
```

If both checks come back clean → swap is verified. The committed change to `config.local.yaml` is local-only (gitignored), so it won't accidentally land in a PR.

**Rollback:** flip `revision` back to `feature/refactor-agent-platform` in `config.local.yaml` and reapply.

### Tier 2: OAM functionality test (the real test of the new content)

Tier 1 only proves the swap is safe. To actually exercise what's new in `feature/oam-for-agents`, three things have to be true:

1. **KubeVela must be installed** — currently it is **not** (verified earlier: target's `bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` has no `kubevela:` entry, and `kubectl get crd | grep oam.dev` would return empty)
2. **The new `oam-agent-components` chart must be applied** — currently **not registered** as an addon (the PR explicitly leaves this for after platform-side KubeVela work)
3. **A test Application using one of the components** must be deployed

Since the platform-side KubeVela provisioning hasn't landed yet, the cleanest way to test today is **manually**, outside the addons mechanism:

```bash
# Step A — install KubeVela manually on hub (one-time, just for testing)
helm repo add kubevela https://kubevela.github.io/charts
helm install --create-namespace -n vela-system kubevela kubevela/vela-core --version 1.10.7 --wait

# Step B — apply the new chart's ComponentDefinitions directly
helm install --namespace vela-system oam-agent-components \
  /Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform/gitops/addons/charts/oam-agent-components

# Verify the 3 ComponentDefinitions are registered
kubectl get componentdefinition -n vela-system agent mcp-server agentcore-memory

# Step C — deploy a minimal test agent
kubectl apply -f /Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform/platform/oam/examples/example-agent-minimal.yaml

# Watch the OAM Application materialize into a Rollout
kubectl get application.core.oam.dev -A
kubectl get rollout -A
```

This is **destructive-ish** for the cluster (installs KubeVela, leaves stuff behind). If this is your dev cluster (it is — `peeks-hub`), that's fine. If you want it cleaner, do it on `spoke-dev` instead — same hub-driven ArgoCD wiring, but the OAM stuff is isolated to the spoke.

### Tier 3: Wire the OAM addon into GitOps (full integration)

This is the "real" deployment path. Two changes needed:

1. **Enable KubeVela** in OAP's bootstrap addons (you noted this is on `feature/agent-platform`, so might already be in flight)
2. **Register `oam-agent-components`** in `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` per the snippet I left in the PR description

Once both land, the addon appears in `enabled-addons.yaml` overlay → flows through ArgoCD → KubeVela ingests the ComponentDefinitions → users can deploy Applications.

This is bigger than a "test" — it's productionizing the feature. Probably right to do as a follow-up PR.

## My recommendation

Run **Tier 1** now to confirm the swap is clean, then do **Tier 2 on spoke-dev** to actually exercise the OAM components. Hold off on Tier 3 until the platform-side KubeVela work in `feature/agent-platform` is locked in.

Want me to:
- **(a)** Run Tier 1 now (need to confirm the exact Taskfile task that renders `agent-platform-app.yaml`), or
- **(b)** Just stage the `config.local.yaml` edit and let you trigger the apply, or
- **(c)** Trace the exact Taskfile task and write a one-shot script for the swap?

The user is pointing out that Tier 3 (full GitOps integration of the OAM addon) wasn't actually completed in the PR, even though they expected it to be. Let me look back at what they originally asked for to understand if this was part of the scope.

Looking at their initial request: the platform provisions KubeVela on hub and spokes, while OAP gets the agentic ComponentDefinitions and other platform-specific files that need to be provisioned. When they said KubeVela comes from the platform and not to worry about the kubevela bootstrap addon, I mistakenly thought that meant *all* addon registration was out of scope. But they were specifically saying the KubeVela addon registration is handled by the platform — the `oam-agent-components` addon registration for our new chart is actually OAP's responsibility and should have been wired up. I conflated the two and missed registering our own addon entirely.

Now I need to verify the PR is missing this registration, add the addon entries to both the bootstrap defaults and the control-plane environment overlay, stage those changes, and then handle the Tier 1 branch swap test by staging the config edit but asking before applying it. Let me start by checking what's currently in the PR and what needs to be added. need to decide whether to use a new label like `enable_oam_agent_components` or reuse the existing `enable_agent_platform` flag that's already set on all three clusters. Since the OAM components should be deployed wherever the agentic platform is enabled, reusing that broader flag makes sense and avoids introducing another label.

For the actual implementation, I'll add the oam-agent-components addon to the bootstrap configuration with the `enable_agent_platform` selector, then enable it in the control-plane environment. The ComponentDefinitions should be registered on all clusters since both hub and spokes might run agent workloads. For the sync wave, I'll use wave 6 or 7 to ensure it runs after KubeVela is installed, without knowing the exact wave the platform uses for KubeVela itself.

Now I'll verify the setup with concrete checks, stage the addon registration changes, and prepare the config.local.yaml edit before applying.

I'm leaning toward a new flag to match the existing addon pattern, though I'm noticing the actual selector structure in OAP's bootstrap configuration isn't immediately clear from what I'm seeing, so I need to examine how kagent handles this since it's the closest analogue with its CRDs and operator pattern.

data.text:
I'm seeing the naming pattern now — feature flags follow the `enable_<feature>` convention with semantic, reusable names across related addons. For the OAM agent components, the flag should be `enable_oam_components` to keep it concise and aligned with the agentic focus of the protocol.

Now I need to think through the deployment strategy: this addon depends on KubeVela being installed first, so I'd set the sync wave to 5 (after KubeVela's wave 3) and place it in the vela-system namespace where ComponentDefinitions typically live. The tricky part is that the control-plane environment uses a different pattern than the dev/prod overlays — the hub uses `useSelectors: true` with ApplicationSets that select by cluster labels, while the spoke environments use an `enabledAddons` map, so I need to figure out how the `enable_oam_components` label flows through the platform Terraform to avoid duplicating the addon configuration across multiple files. Ah, so `useSelectors: false` disables the per-addon selectors and instead uses a global selector — that's why all clusters with `enable_agent_platform: "true"` get the agentic addons regardless of individual addon selectors. Since that label is already set on the clusters I need, I just need to add the addon definition to `bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` and enable it in `environments/control-plane/addons.yaml`, then it'll deploy automatically.

For the edits themselves, I'll add the `oam-agent-components` entry near the agent-gateway addons since they're part of the same agentic platform. For the Tier 1 approach, I'll update the `agenticRepo.revision` in `config.local.yaml` from `feature/refactor-agent-platform` to `feature/oam-for-agents`, stage that change, and ask before applying it.

- **`oam-agent-components` is NOT registered** anywhere in OAP — confirmed missing
- **Sync wave for KubeVela on platform side: 3** (per `feature/oam-for-agents` in appmod)
- **Selector convention**: `enable_<feature>` (e.g. `enable_agent_gateway` is shared across 4 addons)
- **Critical insight on selectors**: `agent-platform-app.yaml` sets `useSelectors: false` with a global selector `enable_agent_platform: "true"`. That label exists on hub + both spokes already → per-addon selectors are overridden, so any addon I add that's enabled in `control-plane/addons.yaml` will deploy to all 3 clusters automatically.

data.text:
I found the bootstrap task that handles the revision flip—it takes environment variables for the repo URL, revision, base path, and cluster name, then substitutes them into the agent platform app manifest and applies it via kubectl.

**Critical finding before applying:** KubeVela is **not installed** on the live cluster.

```
kubectl get crd | grep oam.dev   → empty
kubectl get ns vela-system       → NotFound
```

This affects Tier 1: if you apply with `oam-agent-components: enabled: true` (which is what I just staged), ArgoCD will create the new Application but it will sync to **Degraded** because the `ComponentDefinition` CRD doesn't exist. The error will look like:

```
unable to recognize ".../agent.yaml": no matches for kind "ComponentDefinition" in version "core.oam.dev/v1beta1"
```

This is the cluster state today: the platform-side `feature/agent-platform` branch (which installs KubeVela) isn't deployed yet — the cluster is running the older `feature/agent-platform-shapirov` reference.

## Summary of staged changes

| File | Status | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `gitops/addons/bootstrap/default/addons.yaml` | staged (M) | +18 lines: `oam-agent-components` chart definition at sync-wave 5 |
| `gitops/addons/environments/control-plane/addons.yaml` | staged (M) | +5 lines: `oam-agent-components: enabled: true` |
| `config.local.yaml` | edited (gitignored, local-only) | `agenticRepo.revision: feature/refactor-agent-platform → feature/oam-for-agents` |

The Tier 1 apply command would be: **`task agentic:bootstrap`** (substitutes `${REVISION}` from `AGENTIC_REPO_REVISION` and applies `gitops/fleet/bootstrap/agent-platform-app.yaml`).

## Three options for proceeding

**Option A — Apply as staged. Accept Degraded oam-agent-components apps.**
- Existing 47 apps swap branch cleanly (no-op functionally — branch is additive)
- 3 NEW apps appear (`oam-agent-components-{peeks-hub,spoke-dev,spoke-prod}`) and go Degraded
- Self-resolves once `feature/agent-platform` lands KubeVela
- Honest test of "what happens when this branch goes live"

**Option B — Install KubeVela manually first, then apply Tier 1.**
- Run `helm install -n vela-system --create-namespace kubevela kubevela/vela-core --version 1.10.7 --wait`
- Then run `task agentic:bootstrap`
- Net result: clean Tier 1 swap + functional oam-agent-components on hub
- Caveat: spoke-dev/spoke-prod still don't have KubeVela; their oam-agent-components apps still go Degraded unless we install KubeVela there too
- Trade-off: gives you a real Tier 2 functional test on hub today, but creates two installations of KubeVela (manual + future GitOps-managed) that need to be reconciled later

**Option C — Flip `oam-agent-components: enabled: false` temporarily, apply Tier 1, flip back when KubeVela arrives.**
- Cleanest swap (zero regressions)
- Tier 1 just verifies the additive branch is safe
- The chart definition is in place; one bool flip activates it later
- Doesn't actually exercise the new functionality yet

**Option C** for the immediate Tier 1 test, paired with the platform PR for KubeVela landing first. Then a one-line follow-up commit to flip `enabled: true`. This separates concerns: you verify the branch swap is safe today, the OAM functionality test happens after KubeVela arrives (next week / next platform deploy / however that's sequenced).

If you want to actually exercise the OAM components today on hub, **Option B** is the path — but flag the manual-vs-GitOps reconciliation as a known item.

data.text:
I'm noticing a critical discrepancy: the configuration files show `enable_kubevela: true` across all three clusters (hub, spoke1, and spoke2), yet the actual cluster has no KubeVela CRDs deployed. This suggests the configuration isn't being applied as expected, so I need to trace through the deployment chain to see where it's breaking down.

Looking at the cluster secret labels that were retrieved earlier, I can see all the other enable flags are present (enable_agent_platform, enable_crossplane, enable_external_secrets, etc.), but notably `enable_kubevela` is missing from the labels entirely. This means either the Terraform configuration isn't being applied to this cluster, or the configuration on the branch being deployed doesn't actually match what the user thinks is deployed.

Since the mechanism clearly works for other addons, the issue is likely that the platform Terraform was applied before kubevela was added to hub-config and hasn't been reapplied since. I should check the git history to see when kubevela was actually added to the configuration.

data.text:
KubeVela was added to the hub config back in January 2026, but the cluster is missing the `enable_kubevela` label. This suggests either Terraform was applied after that change without updating the cluster secret for KubeVela, Terraform hasn't been re-applied since the addon was introduced, or something's filtering out the configuration.

Looking at the hub-config addon flags versus what actually appears in the cluster labels, there's a clear mismatch—some flags like `enable_ingress_class_alb`, `enable_argo_workflows`, and `enable_keycloak` have corresponding labels, but many others like `enable_argo_events`, `enable_ingress_nginx`, `enable_backstage`, and `enable_gitlab` don't. I need to check if there's a Terraform transformation that selectively maps addon flags to cluster secret labels, or if the cluster reconciliation is simply out of sync with the hub-config.

input.__tool_use_purpose: Find how hub-config addon flags become cluster secret labels (Terraform mapping)
input.command:
cd /Users/shapirov/projects/appmod-blueprints

echo "=== Search for where addons map to cluster labels ==="
grep -rn "addon\|cluster_addons\|enable_kubevela" platform/infra/terraform/cluster/*.tf platform/infra/terraform/common/*.tf 2>&1 | grep -iE "kubevela|addon" | head -20
echo ""
echo "=== addons.tf or similar ==="
ls platform/infra/terraform/cluster/ 2>&1
echo ""
echo "=== Look at how labels are generated for cluster secret ==="
grep -B 2 -A 10 "addons_metadata\|cluster.*label\|labels.*addon" platform/infra/terraform/common/locals.tf platform/infra/terraform/cluster/*.tf 2>&1 | head -40
echo ""
echo "=== Has Terraform been applied recently? Check terraform.tfstate timestamp ==="
ls -la platform/infra/terraform/cluster/terraform.tfstate* 2>&1 | head -3
ls -la platform/infra/terraform/common/terraform.tfstate* 2>&1 | head -3
echo ""
echo "=== Most recent local state file age (across all terraform dirs) ==="
find platform/infra/terraform -name "terraform.tfstate" -exec ls -la {} \; 2>&1

I'm seeing a critical timeline mismatch: the Terraform state hasn't been updated since mid-February 2026, but we're now in late June—over four months behind. However, kubevela was explicitly enabled in the hub-config back in January, so it should have been provisioned when Terraform was last applied.

The real puzzle is why kubevela and many other addons (kargo, gitlab, ingress_nginx, cert_manager, etc.) aren't showing up as cluster labels at all. Looking at the labels that ARE present, they follow the `enable_` prefix pattern, but there's a significant gap between what's enabled in hub-config and what's actually labeled on the cluster. Either the cluster was last applied before most of these addons were added to the config, or there's some filtering happening in the gitops-bridge module that converts addons to labels.

Let me trace through the Terraform to see what's actually being passed to the cluster secret creation in argocd.tf.

data.text:
So the Terraform configuration hasn't been applied in over four months, while KubeVela was enabled in the config back in January—that's the core issue. The mapping itself is simple: the addon settings just flow directly from the config into the Terraform variables.

The user's config is actually correct; they're pointing at the right branch with `enable_kubevela: true` already set. The problem is that the cluster state is stale because the platform Terraform hasn't been re-applied since February, so those addon changes never made it to the cluster secret labels that ArgoCD needs to see.

The OAP deployments are flowing fine because they use `kubectl apply` directly, not Terraform, which is why the cluster has some recent additions but is missing the newer addon Applications. I need to verify this by checking the cluster labels more carefully.

I've got the full picture now. The user didn't miss anything in `config.local.yaml` since that file only specifies which branches to use, not individual addon settings. The actual `hub-config.yaml` on the deployed branch has `enable_kubevela: true` configured, which is what controls whether the addon is active.

The real issue is that the platform Terraform hasn't been applied since February 13, 2026 — over four months ago. Since then, `hub-config.yaml` has had many addons added or modified (kubevela, kargo, ingress_nginx, cert_manager, jupyterhub, ray_operator, and others), but those changes never made it to the cluster because there's no continuous reconciliation happening. The cluster secret only has 14 addon labels, mostly basic core addons plus one agentic addon, while 17 additional addons that are now enabled in `hub-config.yaml` are missing entirely.

The fix is straightforward: re-run the platform Terraform either via `task platform:upgrade` from the OAP root or directly with `cd ~/.platform && task install`. The main risk is that running Terraform now will trigger installations of all those newly-added addons, and some might fail due to missing chart versions or required secrets, so it's worth being cautious about the timing.

content.data:
Diagnosis complete. **You didn't miss anything in `config.local.yaml`** — that's not where individual addons are toggled. The chain is:

```
config.local.yaml          → just picks the platform branch
        ↓
platform's hub-config.yaml → declares enable_kubevela: true (✓ correct, has been since Jan 23 2026)
        ↓
Terraform apply            → reads hub-config, writes labels onto ArgoCD cluster secret
        ↓
ArgoCD ApplicationSet      → matches enable_kubevela=true label, creates kubevela App
        ↓
KubeVela installs
```

The break is at the **Terraform apply** step. The platform Terraform state is stale:

```
terraform.tfstate last modified: Feb 12-13, 2026
Today:                            Jun 19, 2026
                                  ────────
                                  4+ months stale
```

Meanwhile, **17 addons that are `true` in hub-config never made it to the cluster as labels** — including `enable_kubevela`. The cluster has only the 14 labels that existed at last apply:

| In hub-config (true) but NOT on cluster | On cluster |
|---|---|
| ❌ `enable_kubevela` | ✓ `enable_keycloak` |
| ❌ `enable_kargo` | ✓ `enable_crossplane` |
| ❌ `enable_ingress_nginx` | ✓ `enable_external_secrets` |
| ❌ `enable_cert_manager` | ✓ `enable_grafana_dashboards` |
| ❌ `enable_backstage` | ✓ `enable_argo_workflows` |
| ❌ `enable_ray_operator` | ✓ `enable_metrics_server` |
| ❌ `enable_jupyterhub` | ✓ `enable_ingress_class_alb` |
| ❌ `enable_devlake`, `gitlab`, `kargo`, `kro_manifests_hub`, `argo_events`, `argo_rollouts`, `cni_metrics_helper`, `image_prepuller`, `platform_manifests_*`, `spark_operator`, `crossplane_aws` | ✓ + 7 more |

## Why agentic apps work but platform addons don't

Two completely separate deployment paths:

- **Platform addons (KubeVela, Kargo, Backstage, etc.)** → managed by **Terraform** in `appmod-blueprints`. Has not run in 4 months.
- **Agentic addons (kagent, agentgateway, langfuse, etc.)** → managed by **`task agentic:bootstrap`** (kubectl apply of `agent-platform-app.yaml`). Has been re-run multiple times in recent weeks.

So agentic stuff stays current; platform stuff drifts.

## The fix

Re-run the platform Terraform. Options ordered by blast radius:

**Option 1 — Selective: just enable kubevela**

Pick the smallest possible Terraform run. The addon-to-label mapping happens in the `gitops_bridge_bootstrap` module; running `terraform apply` will reconcile the cluster secret. But Terraform will also try to reconcile **every other drift** — see warning below.

```bash
cd /Users/shapirov/projects/appmod-blueprints/platform/infra/terraform/common
terraform plan      # review carefully — likely shows many addon changes
terraform apply     # only after reviewing
```

**Option 2 — Full platform refresh**

```bash
cd /Users/shapirov/projects/open-agentic-platform
task platform:upgrade    # runs platform's deploy.sh → terraform apply
```

This pulls the latest `feature/agent-platform-shapirov`, configures it, applies Terraform.

## Warning before either option

A 4-month-old state means the plan will likely show **lots** of changes:
- 17 new addon labels added to cluster secrets → 17 new ArgoCD Applications created on hub + spokes
- Some of those addons might pull large charts (Backstage, JupyterHub, GitLab, DevLake) that take resources/time
- Some may fail if secrets they need don't exist (e.g., GitLab token, Keycloak admin secret on a fresh state)
- Could disrupt services that have drifted from declarative state

**My recommendation:** before running `terraform apply`, run `terraform plan` and review. If the plan shows enabling 17 addons all at once feels too risky, narrow `hub-config.yaml` temporarily to enable only what you actually want now (KubeVela + whatever else is essential), apply, then re-add the rest.

## Three reasonable paths forward

1. **Plan + selective apply**: comment out new-and-uninvited addons in hub-config (e.g., set Backstage/JupyterHub/Kargo to false if you don't want them right now), keep `enable_kubevela: true`, run `terraform plan`, review, apply.

2. **Full apply, accept the changes**: review the plan, accept that 17 addons appear, monitor for failures.

3. **Ad-hoc install KubeVela for testing only**: skip Terraform for now, just `helm install kubevela/vela-core` so you can test the OAM addon in PR #18 today. Plan a proper Terraform refresh for later.

Which do you want to do? I'd lean toward **(1)** — gives you control, surfaces drift before applying, lets you do a clean Tier 1 swap with KubeVela actually present afterward.

=== cluster-providers README ===
# Cluster Providers

This directory contains pluggable cluster provisioning approaches. The addon management
system (charts, addons, overlays, fleet, bootstrap) is independent of how the hub
cluster is created.

## Available Providers

| Provider | Description | When to use |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| `kind-crossplane/` | Kind + Crossplane (zero Terraform) | Greenfield, full GitOps |
| `byoc/` | Bring Your Own Cluster | Existing cluster, any cloud provider |

## The Contract

Any provider must produce a running hub cluster that satisfies the conditions below. Once met, the addon management system takes over — the provider's job is done.

### Inputs

| Source | Fields | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `config.yaml` | `hub.clusterName`, `aws.region`, `aws.accountId` | Cluster identity |
| `config.yaml` | `repo.url`, `repo.revision`, `repo.basepath` | Git source for ArgoCD |
| `config.yaml` | `domain`, `resourcePrefix`, `ingressName` | Ingress and naming |
| `config.yaml` | `identityCenter.*`, `argocdCapability.*` | EKS ArgoCD Capability setup |
| `addons/registry/core.yaml` | `argocd.defaultVersion`, `external-secrets.defaultVersion` | Versions (no hardcoding) |
| AWS credentials | IAM permissions | EKS, VPC, IAM, Secrets Manager, Pod Identity |
| `bootstrap/root-appset.yaml` | ApplicationSet manifest | Applied as the final step |

### Outputs

When bootstrap completes, the following must exist:

#### AWS Resources

| Resource | Details |
|----------|---------|
| EKS cluster | Running, accessible via ARN |
| VPC + subnets | Networking for the cluster |
| IAM roles | ArgoCD capability role, ESO pod identity role, Crossplane pod identity role |
| Pod identity associations | ESO and Crossplane mapped to their IAM roles |
| Secrets Manager `<cluster>/config` | Cluster metadata: repo URLs, region, account ID, domain, ingress config |

#### Hub Cluster Resources

| Resource | Namespace | Details |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| ArgoCD | (managed) | EKS ArgoCD Capability running — no pods in `argocd` namespace |
| External Secrets Operator | `external-secrets` | Installed via Helm before ArgoCD can manage it (chicken-and-egg) |
| ClusterSecretStore `aws-secrets-manager` | cluster-scoped | ESO can read from Secrets Manager |
| Seed cluster secret `<cluster>` | `argocd` | See below |
| `root-appset.yaml` | `argocd` | Bootstrap ApplicationSet applied |

#### Seed Cluster Secret

The seed secret is intentionally minimal — just enough for the bootstrap ApplicationSet to target the hub. The fleet-secret chart enriches it later.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: <clusterName>
  namespace: argocd
  labels:
    argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster
    fleet_member: control-plane
    environment: control-plane
  annotations:
    addonsRepoURL: <repo.url>
    addonsRepoRevision: <repo.revision>
```

data.text:
I've identified the root cause: the Kind cluster is running in Podman, but the task is calling `kind get clusters` without setting the `KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman` environment variable, so it defaults to Docker and fails to find the cluster.

The fix is straightforward — I can either export the environment variable for the shell session or pass it inline when running the task. Looking at the rest of the pipeline, most steps use kubectl and Helm which don't depend on Docker, so setting this one variable should unblock the workflow. The Taskfile doesn't need modification since it's not a local-dev concern — the user just needs to export `KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman` before running the task, either as a one-off (`KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman task platform:upgrade`) or persistently in their shell config. Since the `peeks-hub-bootstrap` cluster already exists, the create step will skip and this should smoothly proceed to the addon label upgrade.

content.data:
Found everything:

✅ **Kind cluster is running** — `peeks-hub-bootstrap` is alive in podman
✅ **Podman machine is up** — `podman-machine-default` is "Currently running"
❌ **Kind defaults to Docker** unless told otherwise — that's why it fails

The kind-crossplane task does check "skip if exists" before creating:

```yaml
kind:create:
  desc: Create Kind cluster (skips if exists)
  status:
    - kind get clusters 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^{{.KIND_CLUSTER_NAME}}$"
```

…but `kind get clusters` itself **needs to know to use podman**. Without the env var, kind tries the Docker socket and fails before it even gets to the existence check.

## Fix: one env var

Set `KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman` for the kind CLI. Two options:

**One-shot (just for this run):**
```bash
KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman task platform:upgrade
```

**Persistent (recommended for repeat use):**
```bash
echo 'export KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

That's it. With this set:
- `kind get clusters` will succeed and report `peeks-hub-bootstrap`
- `kind:create` will see it already exists → skip
- The rest of the pipeline (kubectl/helm/aws) doesn't need Docker

## What you should also know

Re-running `task platform:upgrade` will:
1. Skip cluster creation (kind cluster already exists)
2. Re-render `.platform/config.local.yaml`
3. Run platform's full task pipeline — credentials refresh, ArgoCD reconcile, Crossplane setup, etc.
4. Apply hub-config.yaml changes → cluster secret labels for the EKS cluster get updated → the missing 17 enable_* labels (including `enable_kubevela`) appear → KubeVela ApplicationSet matches → KubeVela installs

**No code change needed** in the OAP or platform repos. Just the shell env var.

data.text:
So the bootstrap control plane container crashed three weeks ago with an exit code 137, which points to an out-of-memory kill or forced shutdown. Even though it's still mapped to port 58027 locally, the container isn't running anymore, so there's nothing actually listening on that port—that's why the manifests can't connect and are getting refused.

I could restart the existing container, but after three weeks of being down, there's a real risk that etcd needs recovery or the cluster state is corrupted. The other option is to delete and recreate the kind cluster entirely, though that would mean losing all the bootstrapping state like Crossplane and ArgoCD that's already been set up.

Actually, stepping back—the real question is whether the kind cluster even needs to be running at all. The whole point of it was to provision the EKS cluster initially, which is already done and operating. But looking at the task pipeline, `task platform:upgrade` chains through `kind:create` and then tries to apply things to the kind cluster's API, so the bootstrap cluster is still needed as the control plane for Crossplane to manage the EKS cluster. Any changes to addon enablement flow through the hub config and get applied via Crossplane running in kind.

So the kind cluster has to be running for this to work. I'll recommend starting the container back up, waiting for the API server to come online, verifying it's healthy, and then re-running the upgrade. There are some risks—AWS credentials might have rotated, and the Crossplane state could be stale compared to the actual EKS cluster—but restarting is the simpler path than recreating everything from scratch.

content.data:
Found the real issue. The kind container is **stopped** (exited 3 weeks ago with code 137):

```
peeks-hub-bootstrap-control-plane  ...  Exited (137) 3 weeks ago  127.0.0.1:58027->6443/tcp
```

Port 58027 is its API server, but with the container down, nothing's listening — hence `connection refused`. Kind reports the cluster as "existing" because it sees the container metadata, but it's not actually running.

## Fix: start the container

```bash
podman start peeks-hub-bootstrap-control-plane
```

Then wait ~20–30s for the API server to come up. Verify before re-running the task:

```bash
# 1. Container is up
podman ps --filter "name=peeks-hub-bootstrap-control-plane"

# 2. API server responds (port 58027)
kubectl --context kind-peeks-hub-bootstrap get nodes

# 3. Crossplane and ArgoCD pods come back online
kubectl --context kind-peeks-hub-bootstrap get pods -A | grep -E "crossplane|argocd" | head -10
```

If all three look healthy, re-run:

```bash
KIND_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER=podman task platform:upgrade
```

## Things to watch for after restart

The cluster has been off for 3 weeks — likely outcomes:

- **Pods will restart cleanly** — kind uses local persistent volumes, etcd should recover state
- **AWS credentials may have rotated** — the task includes `credentials:refresh` which should handle this; if it fails, you may need to manually `aws sso login` or refresh creds in your shell first
- **Crossplane state may be stale** — for 3 weeks it didn't reconcile the EKS cluster, so the next reconcile will catch up. Should be benign since EKS state is the source of truth.
- **Some webhooks may fail temporarily** — if you see admission webhook errors, give it another minute

If `podman start` fails with anything weird (out of memory, CNI errors), let me know — there are deeper recovery paths but we should try the simple restart first.
